title: Representation programme for diffeomorphism and current groups
notes: The groups \(G_1=\operatorname{Diff}M\) and \(G_2=H^M\), with smooth maps to a Lie group \(H\), are introduced in connection with describing representations.
statement: For a smooth manifold \(M\) and Lie group \(H\), the current group \(C^\infty(M,H)\) has pointwise multiplication. No representation class, topology, irreducibility criterion or classification theorem is recorded.
reconstruction: This item is a compatibility alias for the identically numbered 1973 occurrence; it is counted once when counting distinct source occurrences.
fate: \citet[title and abstract]{vershikgelfandgraev1975diffeomorphisms} is a relevant later programme, received 15 May 1975 and published in 1975; it does not identify an unrecorded Kirillov theorem. Earlier occurrence: 1973-331.1.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: Automorphisms of a principal bundle and the gauge extension
notes: For a principal \(H\)-bundle \(P\to M\), its automorphisms are said to project onto \(G_1\) with fibre \(G_2\).
statement: There is an exact sequence \(1\to\operatorname{Gau}(P)\to\operatorname{Aut}(P)\to\operatorname{Diff}(M)_P\to1\), where \(\operatorname{Gau}(P)=\Gamma(M,\operatorname{Ad}P)\) and \(\operatorname{Diff}(M)_P=\{f:f^*P\simeq P\}\). For the trivial bundle, the kernel is \(C^\infty(M,H)\) and all base diffeomorphisms lift.
reconstruction: The bundle-preserving subgroup and the adjoint bundle are necessary additions; neither is specified in the shorthand. This item is a compatibility alias for the identically numbered 1973 occurrence; it is counted once when counting distinct source occurrences.
fate: This is the standard bundle-automorphism construction; \citet[abstract and extension sequence]{wockel2007symmetry} formulates it for smooth symmetry groups (preprint December 2006; publication 2007). The construction itself is elementary and predates the talk. Earlier occurrence: 1973-331.2.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Symmetric Fock space
notes: The exponential space is displayed as \(e^H=H_0\oplus H\oplus S^2H\oplus\cdots\), with one-dimensional \(H_0\).
statement: For a complex Hilbert space \(H\), the bosonic Fock space is \(\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sym}^nH\), the Hilbert direct sum with \(\operatorname{Sym}^0H=\mathbb C\).
reconstruction: This item is a compatibility alias for the identically numbered 1973 occurrence; it is counted once when counting distinct source occurrences.
fate: \citet[\S4, pp.~370--373]{araki1970factorizable} uses the exponential Hilbert space in current-group representations; received June 1969, revised November 1969, published 1969/70. Earlier occurrence: 1973-331.3.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Exponential vectors and factorial normalization
notes: Tensor coordinates containing \(\xi^{\otimes n}/n!\) occur beside a norm with weights \(1/n!\). The tensor-product normalization is not stated.
statement: With the usual Hilbert norms on symmetric tensor powers, \(\varepsilon(\xi)=(\xi^{\otimes n}/\sqrt{n!})_{n\ge0}\) satisfies \(\langle\varepsilon(\xi),\varepsilon(\eta)\rangle=e^{\langle\xi,\eta\rangle}\). An equivalent convention places \(1/n!\) in the sector norm and uses coordinates \(\xi^{\otimes n}\).
reconstruction: The two consistent conventions above are an editorial normalization, not an assertion that one specific tensor norm was intended. This item is a compatibility alias for the identically numbered 1973 occurrence; it is counted once when counting distinct source occurrences.
fate: \citet[\S4]{araki1970factorizable} supplies the established exponential-space convention. The displayed factors cannot be combined without specifying a rescaling of each symmetric power. Earlier occurrence: 1973-331.4.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: An unrecorded account of Whitham’s method for KdV
notes: The speaker heading announces KdV by Whitham\textquotesingle s method; no equation, theorem or argument follows.
statement: No mathematically definite assertion can be recovered from this heading alone.
reconstruction: This item is a compatibility alias for the identically numbered 1973 occurrence; it is counted once when counting distinct source occurrences.
fate: \citet[\S1]{gurevichpitaevskii1974shock} is a thematic comparator: submitted 3 April 1973, Russian publication August 1973, English translation February 1974. Its author is A.~V.~Gurevich, whereas this catalogue gives B.~M.; identity and contents are therefore not inferred. Earlier occurrence: 1973-332.1.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: Scalar Hölder regularity for measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients
notes: The names Nash, De Giorgi and Moser accompany the assertion of regularity for one equation; the parenthesis mentions Hölder coefficients.
statement: Let \(u\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\) solve \(\operatorname{div}(A(x)Du)=0\), where \(A\) is bounded measurable and \(\nu|\xi|^2\le \xi^TA(x)\xi\), \(|A(x)|\le\Lambda\). Then \(u\) is locally Hölder continuous. Hölder continuity of \(A\) is unnecessary for this conclusion.
reconstruction: The energy class, local conclusion and uniform bounds have been supplied explicitly.
fate: \citet[\S2, scalar regularity discussion]{mingione2006regularity} records the classical De Giorgi--Nash theory; the central results date from the 1950s, before this talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Using linear theory in scalar nonlinear regularity
notes: The scalar nonlinear situation is described as following the same regularity scheme.
statement: For a uniformly elliptic quasilinear scalar equation, regularity can be bootstrapped once the solution and its gradient lie in a range where the coefficients and their required derivatives are controlled. Smoothness of the coefficient formula alone does not impose those bounds.
reconstruction: No single nonlinear equation is specified. The statement records the valid method and its missing conditions, rather than choosing an unrecorded theorem.
fate: \citet[pp.~111--113]{giusti1982basic} explicitly distinguishes growth hypotheses, minimizers and merely stationary solutions. This is an expository methodological statement, not an unrestricted smoothness theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Failure of scalar regularity for elliptic systems
notes: Giusti and Miranda are associated with an example of a nonregular solution despite analytic coefficients.
statement: There are uniformly elliptic quasilinear systems with real-analytic dependence on the unknown and discontinuous energy-class weak solutions. One corrected concrete example for \(n=N\ge3\) is verified in the companion\textquotesingle s coefficient audit for record 341.
fate: \citet[\S3.2, equations (3.3)--(3.5)]{mingione2006regularity} attributes the analytic-coefficient example to Giusti--Miranda (1968). The original 1968 paper was not retrieved; the later formula and the residual calculation are independently available.
present_status: As of November 2026, the phenomenon is established; the literal tensor later copied on P000565 needs a coefficient emendation.

title: Partial regularity and the dimension of the singular set
notes: The singular set is stated to be closed and to have dimension less than \(n-2\).
statement: For \(n\ge3\), bounded uniformly strongly elliptic \(A(x,v)\), uniformly continuous in \((x,v)\), and an energy weak solution of \(\operatorname{div}(A(x,u)Du)=0\), there is an open regular set on which \(u\) is locally Hölder of every exponent below one; its relatively closed complement has Hausdorff dimension strictly below \(n-2\). The assertion concerns regularity of \(u\), not an unrestricted gradient singular set.
reconstruction: The target is partial regularity of the weak solution, not a universal bound for every nonlinear elliptic system.
fate: \citet[\S1.1, equations (1.1)--(1.2)]{defilippismingionenowak2026partial} states the exact classical local bound and identifies its 1968 foundations. The original arbitrary-order paper \citet{giusti1969partial} was opened but its formula extraction did not permit full verification. The strict inequality is not deduced merely from zero \((n-2)\)-dimensional measure.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed second-order theorem is established; the coefficient and energy hypotheses must be retained.

title: Mean curvature of a graph and a size obstruction
notes: The graph \(x\mapsto u(x)\) is assigned mean curvature \(n^{-1}\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2})\); prescribed curvature cannot be arbitrarily large.
statement: For an oriented \(C^2\) graph over \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\), the signed average principal curvature is \(n^{-1}\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2})\), up to orientation. Integrating the divergence over a subdomain bounds total prescribed curvature by boundary area.
fate: \citet[\S1B]{giusti1976boundary} develops the associated perimeter condition. The flux obstruction is elementary and already part of the pre-1974 mean-curvature existence theory; record 338 gives its explicit form.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Complex tori and algebraic tori
notes: A torus is written \(\mathbb C^n/\Lambda\), where \(\Lambda\) has a basis of \(2n\) vectors; algebraic tori are called abelian varieties.
statement: A complex torus is \(\mathbb C^g/\Lambda\) for a discrete lattice of rank \(2g\) spanning the real vector space. It is an abelian variety precisely when it is projective, equivalently when it admits a positive Riemann form. Here “algebraic torus” means a projective complex torus, not the affine group \((\mathbb C^*)^g\).
fate: \citet[complex tori and Riemann forms]{milne2008abelian} gives the classical criterion. The terminology in these notes is historical and should not be confused with an algebraic group torus.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The unspecified problem of describing all tori
notes: Novikov asks how to describe all tori, noting that dimension two is already nontrivial.
statement: The notebook does not say whether tori are polarized, whether isomorphism or isogeny is intended, or whether the aim is a parameter space, a Jacobian criterion or explicit functions. No unique definite problem follows.
fate: The marked hyperelliptic-Jacobian construction of \citet[\S4]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} is a precise nearby result, submitted 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974. It does not settle every possible interpretation of the question.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: Hyperelliptic curves and their holomorphic differentials
notes: The curve \(y^2=P_{2g+1}(x)\) is used with the forms \(x^kdx/y\).
statement: If \(P_{2g+1}\in\mathbb C[x]\) has distinct roots, the smooth projective compactification of \(y^2=P_{2g+1}(x)\) has genus \(g\); \(x^kdx/y\), \(0\le k\le g-1\), is a basis of holomorphic differentials. Repeated roots require normalization and can lower the genus.
reconstruction: Square-freeness, compactification and the index range have been made explicit.
fate: This classical construction is the input to \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, not a new assertion of that paper.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The Jacobian and the missing Hodge quotient
notes: The Jacobian is written \(H^1(R,\mathbb C)/H^1(R,\mathbb Z)\).
statement:
For a compact Riemann surface \(R\) of genus \(g\), \(J(R)=H^0(R,\Omega_R^1)^*/H_1(R,\mathbb Z)\), with the lattice embedded by integration. Equivalently,
\[J(R)=H^1(R,\mathbb C)/(F^1H^1(R,\mathbb C)+H^1(R,\mathbb Z)).\] The literal quotient omits a complex \(g\)-dimensional Hodge subspace.
fate: \citet[\S2, analytic description]{milne1986jacobian} gives the period construction. The omission is mathematical: the literal numerator has complex dimension \(2g\) and its rank-\(2g\) lattice does not give the compact Jacobian.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Period matrices and the moduli diagram
notes: A diagram relates curves, tori, periods and a domain of matrices.
statement: After a symplectic marking and normalization, a principally polarized complex abelian variety is represented by a symmetric matrix \(\tau\) with \(\operatorname{Im}\tau>0\). Changing the marking acts by \(\operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)\). The resulting quotient describes principally polarized abelian varieties; the period map from curves lands in the Jacobian locus.
reconstruction: Principal polarization and marking are editorial additions required to identify the matrix domain.
fate: \citet[polarizations and moduli]{milne2008abelian} supplies the standard setting. The diagram does not specify a level structure or a fine moduli space, and its arrows are not treated as unqualified isomorphisms.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: A genus-two polynomial Hamiltonian pair and its corrected quartic coefficient
notes: The notes give \(J_1=p_1p_2+V\), \(J_2=p_1^2-2q_1p_1p_2+2(q_2-c)p_2^2+D\), claiming \(\{J_1,J_2\}=0\), where the quartic term of \(V\) is \(-5q_1^4/2\).
statement: Identify \(c=c_1,d=d_1\) and put \[V_a=-\tfrac12q_2^2-\tfrac52q_1^2q_2-aq_1^4+cq_1^2-dq_1,\quad D=q_1^5+2cq_1^3+dq_1^2-4q_1q_2^2+4cq_1q_2-2dq_2.\] For \(\{f,g\}=\sum_i(f_{q_i}g_{p_i}-f_{p_i}g_{q_i})\), direct calculation gives \(\{J_1,J_2\}=(8a-5)q_1^3(q_1p_2-p_1)\). Thus the copied coefficient \(a=5/2\) fails, while \(a=5/8\) works.
reconstruction: The identification of the differently subscripted parameters is explicit. The replacement concerns the last quartic coefficient only.
fate: \citet[\S2, equations (18)--(19), p.~64]{novikov1974periodic} already publishes the genus-two Hamiltonian construction (received 18 February 1974; publication July 1974), before this September talk. The coefficient is also \(5/8\) after expanding \citet[\S4]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}. The exact bracket audit below verifies the mathematical correction in the notebook convention.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected classical commuting pair is established; the printed notebook pair is not in involution.

title: Commuting Hamiltonian vector fields
notes: The two Hamiltonian fields are asserted to commute.
statement: On a symplectic manifold, \([X_f,X_g]=\pm X_{\{f,g\}}\), with sign determined by convention. Consequently the corrected pair in item 1974-336.6 has commuting Hamiltonian fields. The uncorrected pair generally does not.
fate: This is the standard Hamiltonian identity used in \citet[\S2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}. The application is contingent on the coefficient correction, not a second independent assertion of involution.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Common levels as open parts of abelian varieties
notes: The common levels \(J_1,J_2=\mathrm{constant}\) and flow orbits are called tori or abelian varieties.
statement: For the corrected genus-two stationary-KdV system and generic constants giving a nonsingular spectral curve, the affine common level is identified with a Zariski-open part of its Jacobian. The complete abelian surface is obtained by compactification. Compact nonsingular real components support the real torus dynamics; arbitrary complex affine levels are not compact tori.
reconstruction: Genericity and compactification are necessary. Singular spectral curves require a separate degeneration theory.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--4]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} and \citet[Ch.~II, \S4]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} give the finite-gap algebraic-integrability construction (1974 result; 1976 synthesis).
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Rational parametrization of the marked universal hyperelliptic Jacobian
notes: The collection of all the preceding tori is said to be unirational.
statement: The precise nearby construction concerns a total family of hyperelliptic Jacobians, with a distinguished branch point and the coordinate/marking normalizations used in its polynomial model. It is a rational total parameter variety in that formulation, hence gives a unirational family after forgetting the finite marking. This does not make any fixed positive-dimensional complex abelian variety unirational.
reconstruction: The family and its marking have been supplied from the matching result; an arbitrary fine-moduli interpretation is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S4, theorem]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} states rationality of the marked total variety; the manuscript is its abbreviated geometric consequence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The spectral quintic and a parameter-normalization discrepancy
notes: The curve is written \[y^2=E^5+\tfrac c4E^3-\tfrac d{16}E^2+(\tfrac{J_1}{32}+\tfrac{c^2}{4})E+\tfrac{J_2}{256}+\tfrac{cd}{128}.\]
statement: The spectral construction is established, but its coefficients depend on the Hamiltonian and spectral-coordinate normalization. With the repaired \(J_1\), canonical flow \(D_x=\{\cdot,J_1\}\), \(u=q_1\), and \(P=E^2+q_1E/2+(q_1^2-2q_2+2c)/16\), exact substitution into the squared-eigenfunction identity gives \[R=E^5+\tfrac c4E^3-\tfrac d{16}E^2+(\tfrac{J_1}{32}+\tfrac{c^2}{64})E-\tfrac{J_2}{256}-\tfrac{cd}{128}.\] This is a conditional normalization check; it does not establish a literal corrected reading of the notebook.
reconstruction: The author-hosted Dubrovin--Novikov parameter change yields \(c^2/64\), but that text also prints a positive constant term and has apparent typographic defects elsewhere. The notebook does not specify its Lax matrix. The conditional computation fixes the coefficients only after the stated choices of potential, flow and divisor polynomial.
fate: \citet[\S2, equation (18)]{novikov1974periodic} already publishes the genus-two spectral polynomial in July 1974. Compare \citet[\S4]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} and the coordinate interpretation in \citet[Ch.~II, \S4, p.~105]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The companion gives an exact conditional polynomial audit, while preserving the unresolved comparison of all source normalizations.
present_status: As of November 2026, the spectral construction is established, and the stated normalization has been checked exactly; the literal coefficient and constant-term comparison remains an explicitly unresolved normalization discrepancy.

title: Abel’s map from a symmetric power
notes: The map \(S^gR\to J(R)\), given by sums of integrals of holomorphic differentials from a base point, is called an isomorphism.
statement: For a smooth projective complex curve of genus \(g\), \(D\mapsto[D-gQ]\) maps \(\operatorname{Sym}^gR\) surjectively and birationally to \(J(R)\). Its fibre over \([D-gQ]\) is the complete linear system \(|D|\). Thus it is an isomorphism on the nonspecial locus, but generally not globally: in genus two the hyperelliptic pencil gives a positive-dimensional fibre.
fate: \citet[Theorem~5.1 and the preceding fibre description]{milne1986jacobian} states the classical result. The source is a 2021 corrected version of the 1986 chapter; the mathematical theorem long predates this lecture.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Normalized Bloch solutions and the unit multiplier condition
notes: For \(L=-d^2/dx^2+u\), the notes impose \(\Psi(x+T)=\lambda\Psi(x)\), \(|\lambda|=1\), \(\lambda=e^{ip}\), and \(\Psi(x_0)=1\).
statement: For a real smooth \(T\)-periodic potential, Floquet solutions satisfy \(\Psi(x+T,E)=\lambda(E)\Psi(x,E)\). The condition \(|\lambda|=1\) characterizes real spectral bands; it is not true in open gaps. Normalization at \(x_0\) is meromorphic in the spectral point and fails as an ordinary finite value at its pole divisor.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} sets out the standard Floquet normalization used in the new finite-gap construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The almost-periodic completeness warning
notes: For almost-periodic potentials the collection of such eigenfunctions is said not to form a complete system.
statement: An almost-periodic function need not have a period \(T\), so the preceding monodromy eigenvalue equation does not define a general Bloch basis. No function space, spectral measure or notion of completeness is specified here.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} distinguishes the periodic case from an imposed meromorphic finite-gap condition in the conditionally periodic case. This does not identify an exact completeness counterexample.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: The two-sheeted spectral surface and its genus
notes: Two eigenfunctions lead to a two-sheeted surface branched at spectral endpoints, described as having infinite genus.
statement: The normalized Bloch functions for a real periodic Schrödinger operator are naturally considered on a two-sheeted spectral surface. Open-gap endpoints are branch points; closed gaps give removable double points after normalization. Infinitely many open gaps give an infinite-genus surface. With \(g\) open gaps, the compact finite-gap model is \(y^2=\prod_{j=0}^{2g}(E-E_j)\), of genus \(g\).
reconstruction: The qualifier “infinitely many open gaps” is necessary; periodicity alone does not imply infinite genus.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} distinguishes the general periodic surface from its finite-gap algebraic specialization.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The finite-gap isospectral family and its Jacobian
notes: The set of potentials with the same spectrum is identified with the Jacobian of the spectral surface.
statement: Fix a real nonsingular finite-gap spectrum with \(g\) open gaps and admissible real divisor data. The corresponding smooth real isospectral family is a real \(g\)-torus in the complex Jacobian. The complex algebraic construction is described on an open Jacobian chart and its compactification. Infinite-gap spectra require additional analytic hypotheses and do not give this finite-dimensional statement.
reconstruction: The finite-gap and real-admissibility conditions are made explicit.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} gives the finite-gap identification and linearized flows; publication followed the September lecture in 1974, with receipt on 3 June 1974.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Z-sets defined by approximation of Hilbert-cube maps
notes: A closed subset \(A\) of a complete metric space \(X\) is called a Z-set if continuous maps of the Hilbert cube can be approximated by maps missing \(A\).
statement: For a metric space \(X\), a closed subset \(A\subset X\) is a Z-set in the stated sense if for every continuous \(f:Q\to X\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is continuous \(g:Q\to X\setminus A\) with \(\sup_Qd(f,g)<\varepsilon\), where \(Q=[-1,1]^{\mathbb N}\).
fate: \citet[introduction, pp.~281--282]{andersonchapman1971extending} recalls the established negligible-set theory and its equivalent formulations in Hilbert-cube manifolds. The ambient-space hypotheses matter when moving between those formulations.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The pseudoboundary of the Hilbert cube
notes: For \(Q=[-1,1]^{\mathbb N}\) and \(P=(-1,1)^{\mathbb N}\), the notes call \(Q\setminus P\) a Z-set.
statement: The pseudoboundary is \(\bigcup_{j\ge1}\{x\in Q:|x_j|=1\}\), a countable union of closed Z-sets. It is dense and not closed in \(Q\), so it is not itself a Z-set under the preceding definition. Each coordinate face can be avoided by an arbitrarily small inward change in that coordinate.
fate: The distinction is part of the Hilbert-cube setting of \citet[pp.~281--282]{andersonchapman1971extending}; the correction also follows immediately from the definition copied in the notes.
present_status: As of November 2026, the pseudoboundary is a sigma-Z-set, and the literal Z-set claim is false.

title: Z-set unknotting in the Hilbert cube
notes: A homeomorphism between two Z-sets extends to a homeomorphism of the surrounding cube.
statement: If \(A,B\) are closed Z-sets in the Hilbert cube \(Q\), every homeomorphism \(h:A\to B\) extends to a homeomorphism \(H:Q\to Q\).
reconstruction: The ambient Hilbert cube is essential; the preceding definition for arbitrary complete metric spaces does not make the extension assertion true there.
fate: \citet[Theorem~4 and corollary, pp.~37--38]{anderson1967special} gives the extension theorem in its equivalent deficient-set formulation; \citet[introduction]{andersonchapman1971extending} explicitly recalls Z-set unknotting. Both precede the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Countable unions of Z-sets
notes: A \(Z_\sigma\)-set is introduced as a countable union of Z-sets.
statement: A sigma-Z-set in \(X\) is a set \(A=\bigcup_{m\ge1}A_m\) with each \(A_m\) a closed Z-set in \(X\). The union need not be closed.
fate: This is standard negligible-set terminology in the infinite-dimensional topology discussed by \citet[pp.~31--38]{anderson1967special}. The pseudoboundary is the preceding concrete example.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The ambiguous maximal sigma-Z-set assertion
notes: The notes say that a maximal \(Z_\sigma\)-set exists.
statement: If maximal means maximal by inclusion among sigma-Z-subsets of \(Q\), the claim is false. Every Z-set is nowhere dense, so a sigma-Z-set is meagre and is not \(Q\). Any missing point is itself a Z-set, and adjoining it gives a strictly larger sigma-Z-set. A universal or absorbing-set meaning would require an additional definition.
fate: The literal obstruction follows from the Baire theorem and the preceding definition. Searches in the opened Anderson and Anderson--Chapman sources did not identify a theorem with the unqualified maximality stated here.
present_status: As of November 2026, inclusion-maximality is refuted; an intended absorbing or universal notion is not recoverable from this sentence.

title: Every continuous real function on the ray space is constant
notes: Gelfand considers rays in the space of real sequences and says that every continuous function on the quotient is constant.
statement: Let \(X=\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\) have its product topology and let \(S=(X\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb R_{>0}\) be the quotient by positive scalar multiplication. Every continuous \(S\to\mathbb R\) is constant. Equivalently, every continuous degree-zero homogeneous real function on \(X\setminus\{0\}\) is constant.
reconstruction: The product topology and positive scaling are essential. A normed-space unit sphere gives a different quotient.
fate: \citet[introduction, Russian p.~34]{gelfandfuchs1967topology} states this exact example; received July 1967, published 1967. The space is described there as Hausdorff but nonregular, not as a non-Hausdorff quotient. Earlier occurrence: 1967-132.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Homeomorphism type of infinite-dimensional separable Fréchet spaces
notes: All separable Fréchet spaces are said to be homeomorphic.
statement: All infinite-dimensional separable real Fréchet spaces are homeomorphic to separable Hilbert space. Finite-dimensional spaces are excluded: their topological dimensions distinguish them from one another and from the infinite-dimensional case.
fate: \citet[p.~31]{anderson1967special} explicitly summarizes the already established Anderson--Kadec and related results. The 1966 symposium paper appeared in 1967, before this talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The prescribed-mean-curvature Dirichlet equation
notes: The equation is \(\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2})=-H(x,u)\), with \(u=\phi\) on the boundary; \(H=0\) is the minimal-surface case.
statement: Given a bounded domain \(\Omega\), boundary data \(\phi\) and prescribed function \(H\), seek an appropriately defined solution of the displayed graph equation with the stated boundary trace. Classical, weak Sobolev and relaxed BV solutions are different formulations; none exists for arbitrary data without additional conditions.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S1]{giusti1976boundary} treats the generalized Dirichlet formulation and recalls the earlier work on existence. The lecture\textquotesingle s examples establish why the solution class must be stated.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: A radial annulus and the maximal catenoid height
notes: On \(1<|x|<2\subset\mathbb R^2\), radial minimal graphs have inner value \(M\) and outer value zero; beyond \(M_0\) no solution exists.
statement: For \(0\le c\le1\), the radial solutions are \[u_c(r)=c\log\frac{2+\sqrt{4-c^2}}{r+\sqrt{r^2-c^2}}.\] Their heights increase to \(M_0=\log(2+\sqrt3)\). There is no \(C^2(\Omega)\cap C^0(\overline\Omega)\) minimal graph with these boundary values if \(M>M_0\): comparison gives uniqueness, rotation invariance forces radiality, and \(ru^{\prime}/\sqrt{1+(u^{\prime})^2}=-c\) forces \(c\le1\). At equality the inner-boundary slope is infinite.
reconstruction: The solution class and the equality case are editorially explicit; \(C^1\) regularity up to the inner boundary fails at \(c=1\).
fate: This is an explicit catenoid calculation illustrating the classical-versus-generalized distinction in \citet[introduction]{giusti1976boundary}. Its exact formula and threshold follow directly by integrating the radial equation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Soap-film diagrams as a geometric illustration
notes: Drawings show a film lifted with a rod and a film spanning wire rings, accompanying an experimental check of loss of graph solvability.
statement: The drawings illustrate the distinction between a single-valued graph over an annulus and a general spanning surface. They specify no surface functional, stability criterion, contact-angle condition or exact transition height for the physical experiment.
fate: The neighbouring radial calculation is identifiable, but no precise theorem about the drawn experiment is recorded. The general variational background in \citet[introduction]{giusti1976boundary} is thematic only.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: A continuous prescribed curvature with an infinite-slope solution
notes: The example \(u(x)=3x^{1/3}\), \(-1<x<1\), is nondifferentiable at zero although the derivative of its curvature flux is continuous.
statement: Using the real cube root, \(u\in W^{1,1}(-1,1)\) and \(u^{\prime}=|x|^{-2/3}\) almost everywhere. Its flux is \(q=(1+|x|^{4/3})^{-1/2}\), with \(q^{\prime}=-(2/3)\sqrt[3]{x}(1+|x|^{4/3})^{-3/2}\), a continuous function. Thus a weak graph solution may have continuous right-hand side without finite slope. It is not in \(W^{1,2}\).
fate: The assertion is verified by direct differentiation and integrability at zero; it illustrates the degeneracy explained by \citet[\S1]{giusti1976boundary}. No exact published formula match was found.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Raising one endpoint beyond the possible flux
notes: After \(u(-1)=-3,u(1)=3\), the notes change to \(u(-1)=3,u(1)=3+A\) but integrate from the value \(-3\).
statement: For the fixed right-hand side of item 1974-338.4, retain \(v(-1)=-3\). Any admissible flux is \(q_v=q+C\). Since \(q(0)=1\) and \(|q_v|\le1\), necessarily \(C\le0\); monotonicity of \(s/\sqrt{1+s^2}\) gives \(v^{\prime}\le |x|^{-2/3}\). Therefore \(v(1)\le3\), and data \(v(1)=3+A\), \(A>0\), are impossible.
reconstruction: The left endpoint is restored to \(-3\), and the omitted integration constant is included. The equality flux corresponds to a weak solution with infinite slope.
fate: This is the elementary one-dimensional obstruction adjacent to the explicit example. The general perimeter obstruction is treated by \citet[\S1B]{giusti1976boundary}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The area-plus-potential functional and its Euler equation
notes: The functional is \(\mathcal F(u)=\int_\Omega\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}+\int_\Omega\lambda(x,u)\), with \(\lambda_t=H\).
statement: For smooth admissible variations with fixed boundary values, the displayed plus sign gives \(-\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2})+H(x,u)=0\), hence \(\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2})=H(x,u)\). To match the earlier equation with \(-H\), use \(-\lambda\) or redefine the sign of \(H\).
fate: The first variation is immediate. \citet[\S1]{giusti1976boundary} uses a consistent area-plus-volume convention; the notebook switches conventions without warning.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Removing the gradient cutoff in variational minimization
notes: A minimum is asserted under \(|Du|\le K\); then the notes ask whether the minimizers \(u_K\) converge as \(K\to\infty\).
statement: On a bounded Lipschitz domain with nonempty fixed-trace admissible class, a fixed uniform gradient bound and suitable continuity of the potential give a direct-method minimum. Removing the bound requires a uniform BV and \(L^1\) estimate. It is false without coercivity: if \(H=h>0\) is sufficiently large and \(w\ge0\) has zero trace with \(h\int w>\int|Dw|\), then \(\mathcal F(-tw)\to-\infty\). Under a coercive relaxed functional, subsequences converge in \(L^1\) to BV minimizers, which need not retain the classical boundary values.
reconstruction: The coercivity and boundary assumptions are not present in the question. The elementary large-force counterexample shows why they cannot be omitted.
fate: \citet[introduction and existence hypotheses]{giusti1976boundary} explains the BV setting and necessary size restrictions. The unqualified convergence question has no affirmative answer; the positive compactness argument is supplied by the subsequent items.
present_status: As of November 2026, the conditional BV approach is classical; unconditional convergence is false and no separate open problem is inferred.

title: A necessary flux-perimeter inequality
notes: For a Lipschitz solution and \(A\subset\Omega\), the notes bound \(|\int_AH|\) by \((1-\varepsilon_0)\mathcal H^{n-1}(\partial A)\).
statement: If \(u\) is a solution with \(\|Du\|_\infty\le K<\infty\), then for every smooth relatively compact subdomain \(A\), \[\left|\int_AH(x,u(x))\,dx\right|\le\frac{K}{\sqrt{1+K^2}}\mathcal H^{n-1}(\partial A).\] The same statement has a finite-perimeter formulation using normal traces. The sign convention disappears after taking absolute values.
fate: \citet[\S1B]{giusti1976boundary} treats the same geometric obstruction. The constant in the notebook is precisely the supremum norm of the flux.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Bounded variation and the dual definition of total variation
notes: BV functions are \(L^1\) functions whose first distributional derivatives are Radon measures, with a dual supremum over bounded test vector fields.
statement: For an open \(\Omega\), \(u\in BV(\Omega)\) means \(u\in L^1(\Omega)\) and \[|Du|(\Omega)=\sup_{g\in C_c^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^n),\ |g|\le1}\int_\Omega u\operatorname{div}g\,dx<\infty.\] This is equivalent to the distributional gradient being a finite vector Radon measure.
fate: \citet[\S1A]{giusti1976boundary} recalls the standard definition used in the earlier area-relaxation theory.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Relaxed area for a BV graph
notes: The notation \(\int\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}\) is defined through a supremum over \((g_0,g)\) satisfying \(g_0^2+|g|^2\le1\).
statement: If \(Du=\nabla u\,dx+D^su\), the relaxed area is \[\mathcal A(u)=\int_\Omega\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}\,dx+|D^su|(\Omega).\] It equals \(\sup\int_\Omega(g_0+u\operatorname{div}g)\,dx\) over compactly supported \(C^1\) test fields with \(g_0^2+|g|^2\le1\). It is not obtained by squaring a singular measure as a density.
fate: \citet[\S1A]{giusti1976boundary} gives this generalized-area formulation; the notebook\textquotesingle s dual definition is the appropriate interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Lower semicontinuity of BV area
notes: The area is lower semicontinuous for \(L^1\) convergence.
statement: If \(u_j\to u\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\), then \(\mathcal A(u)\le\liminf_j\mathcal A(u_j)\), with the area extended by \(+\infty\) outside \(BV\). Each functional in the dual supremum is \(L^1\)-continuous, and a supremum of such functions is lower semicontinuous.
fate: \citet[\S1A]{giusti1976boundary} uses this standard direct-method fact. The dual formula in the notes supplies its proof.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Compactness of bounded BV sets
notes: Bounded sets in BV are said to be relatively compact in \(L^1\).
statement: If \(\Omega\) is bounded with Lipschitz boundary and \(\sup_j(\|u_j\|_{L^1}+|Du_j|(\Omega))<\infty\), there is an \(L^1(\Omega)\)-convergent subsequence. On a general open set only local compactness follows without control at infinity and the boundary. Bounding total variation alone does not control additive constants.
reconstruction: The domain condition and the full BV norm are essential additions.
fate: \citet[\S1A]{giusti1976boundary} states the bounded-domain framework in which the BV compactness argument is applied.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Boundary mismatch in the relaxed Dirichlet functional
notes: The area-plus-potential expression acquires \(\int_{\partial\Omega}|u-\phi|\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}\).
statement: For a bounded Lipschitz domain, BV trace \(Tu\) and integrable boundary datum \(\phi\), the generalized Dirichlet energy contains \[\mathcal A(u)+\int_\Omega\lambda(x,u)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}|Tu-\phi|\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}.\] This boundary term permits detachment from the prescribed trace while charging its vertical area. Existence still requires lower semicontinuity and coercivity of the entire functional.
fate: \citet[pp.~501--505]{giusti1976boundary} explicitly recalls generalized-solution constructions from Giusti (1970), Giaquinta and Miranda (1973--1974). This framework was already available at the talk; the 1976 paper studies its boundary behaviour.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The finite-gap hyperelliptic spectral curve
notes: For a finite-gap potential, \(R(E)=\prod(E-E_i)\) and \(\Gamma_N\) is the surface of \(\sqrt{R(E)}\); \(N\) is its genus.
statement: For a real smooth periodic Schrödinger potential with exactly \(N\) open gaps, list the distinct finite band endpoints \(E_1<\cdots<E_{2N+1}\). The smooth compactification of \(y^2=\prod_{j=1}^{2N+1}(E-E_j)\) has genus \(N\). Closed gaps are omitted after normalization.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} gives the algebraic spectral construction (received June 1974, published 1974). The hyperelliptic genus count itself is classical.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Meromorphic continuation of the normalized Bloch solution
notes: Bloch functions continue analytically, corrected to meromorphically, on \(\Gamma_N\setminus\{\infty\}\).
statement: With \(\Psi(x_0,E,x_0)=1\), the finite-gap Bloch solution at fixed \(x\) is meromorphic on the spectral curve away from the point above infinity. In the local parameter \(k=\sqrt E\), its exponential factor is \(e^{\pm ik(x-x_0)}\); infinity is generally an essential singularity.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} states the continuation result; \citet[\S\S1--2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodic} develops the eigenfunction construction (submitted July 1974, Russian publication December 1974).
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Pole and zero divisors of degree N with possible cancellation
notes: The function is said to have \(N\) poles \(\gamma_i(x_0)\) and \(N\) zeros.
statement: There are effective degree-\(N\) divisors \(D(x_0)\) and \(D(x)\) such that the finite divisor of the normalized solution is \(D(x)-D(x_0)\), with common points cancelling. Generically the poles and zeros each number \(N\), with multiplicity; at \(x=x_0\), \(\Psi\equiv1\) and all cancel.
fate: The divisor construction is in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}. The cancellation qualification follows already from the normalization and prevents a false universal exact count.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: One divisor point on each real gap oval
notes: Each oval projects to a forbidden gap and carries one pole and one zero; poles depend on \(x_0\).
statement: For the real nonsingular finite-gap class, each admissible Dirichlet divisor has one point on each real oval above a closed finite gap interval, with its sheet specified and the two sheets meeting at endpoints. \(D(x_0)\) is the pole divisor and \(D(x)\) the moving zero divisor before cancellation.
reconstruction: The assertion concerns admissible real data, not arbitrary complex divisors.
fate: \citet[\S3, the points \(\gamma_j\)]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} gives the gap and sheet description; \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} supplies its detailed spectral formulation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Periodic Schrödinger bands and finite-gap potentials
notes: The spectrum of \(L=-d^2/dx^2+u(x)\), \(u(x+T)=u(x)\), is a union of intervals; finitely many bands is called finite-zone.
statement: For real smooth \(T\)-periodic \(u\), the self-adjoint operator on \(L^2(\mathbb R)\) has a closed band spectrum. A finite-gap potential has finitely many open bounded gaps, so its spectrum consists of finitely many compact bands and a final half-line, with closed gaps filled in.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} recalls this classical spectral setting before describing the 1974 finite-gap theory.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Unimodular monodromy and its characteristic equation
notes: Translation by \(T\) acts on a solution basis through \(\widehat T=(\alpha_{ij})\); the Wronskian gives determinant one.
statement: For \(-y^{\prime\prime}+uy=Ey\), a fundamental solution matrix normalized at \(x_0\) has monodromy \(M(E,x_0)\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\). If \(\tau=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}M\), its multipliers satisfy \(\lambda^2-2\tau\lambda+1=0\). The determinant is one because the Wronskian is constant.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1, monodromy construction]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} records these classical identities.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The bounded-solution and discriminant criterion for the spectrum
notes: A spectral point has a bounded solution, hence a monodromy eigenvalue of modulus one; \(|\operatorname{tr}M|<2\) gives complex roots and \(>2\) real roots.
statement: For real \(E\), \(E\in\sigma(L)\) if and only if \(|\tau(E)|\le1\), equivalently there is a nonzero solution bounded on all of \(\mathbb R\). In band interiors the multipliers are conjugate on the unit circle; in open gaps they are distinct real reciprocals. At an endpoint a bounded periodic or antiperiodic solution exists even when a second solution grows linearly.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives the Floquet spectral criterion. The endpoint qualification distinguishes one bounded eigenvector from boundedness of every monodromy iterate.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Quasimomentum and the Bloch multiplier
notes: The Bloch condition is written using \(u\), with \(\nu=e^{ip}\) and \(p\) called quasimomentum.
statement: For a Bloch solution \(\psi\), write \(\psi(x+T,E)=e^{ip(E)}\psi(x,E)\). The phase \(p\) is defined modulo \(2\pi\) and a choice of the reciprocal multiplier; on spectral bands it can be chosen real. The symbol \(u\) in that line denotes the eigenfunction, although elsewhere it denotes the potential.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} fixes the same Floquet phase convention, subject to a possible factor \(T\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Base-point independence of the discriminant
notes: The half-trace \(\tau(E)\) does not depend on the normalization point \(x_0\).
statement: Monodromy matrices at different base points are conjugate by the intervening fundamental solution matrix. Their trace and multipliers are therefore independent of \(x_0\), although the individual matrix entries and normalized eigenvectors are not.
fate: This standard conjugacy argument underlies \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Bloch continuation to the finite-gap curve
notes: Theorem 1 says that Bloch eigenfunctions analytically continue to \(\Gamma_N\), with normalization one at \(x_0\).
statement: For a real nonsingular finite-gap potential, the normalized Bloch function extends meromorphically to \(\Gamma_N\setminus\{\infty\}\), with fixed pole divisor and an essential exponential singularity at infinity. ``Analytic continuation is not a claim of holomorphy at its poles or at infinity.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} is the matching 1974 result; this repeats items 1974-339.2--4 in a longer proof-oriented lecture.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Finite-gap potentials are stationary for a higher KdV equation
notes: Theorem 0 states that every finite-zone potential is a stationary solution of a higher KdV equation.
statement: For a real smooth periodic Schrödinger potential, having finitely many open gaps is equivalent to satisfying a nontrivial stationary equation in the KdV hierarchy, allowing a finite linear combination of the flows and integration constants. Equivalently, there is an odd-order differential operator commuting with \(L\) of the corresponding finite-gap type.
fate: \citet[\S2 and the converse at the end of \S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} gives both directions, referring the stationary-to-finite-gap direction to \citet{novikov1974periodic}. Novikov\textquotesingle s paper was received February 1974; the joint paper June 1974; both appeared in 1974. Earlier related occurrence: 1973-326.15.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The Jacobian description of the isospectral manifold
notes: Theorem 2 calls the set of potentials with fixed spectrum \(J(\Gamma_N)\).
statement: For a fixed nonsingular finite-gap curve, admissible real divisor data identify the smooth real isospectral family with a real \(N\)-torus. Complex divisor coordinates identify an open part of the complexified construction with an open part of \(J(\Gamma_N)\), whose compactification is the Jacobian.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} supplies the algebraic-geometric identification. The real/complex and affine/compact distinctions refine the lecture\textquotesingle s shorthand.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Higher KdV flows on the isospectral Jacobian
notes: KdV and its higher analogues act on the fixed-spectrum manifold.
statement: The commuting hierarchy flows preserve the spectral curve and become constant-velocity translations in Abel coordinates on its Jacobian. On the admissible real component these are commuting flows on a real torus; periodicity in a particular time requires additional rationality of the velocity vector.
fate: \citet[\S3, Abel coordinates]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} and \citet[\S\S2--3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodic} identify these flows (1974 submissions and publications).
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Monotonicity of a chosen band phase
notes: The roots are said to run in one direction, with a parenthetical remark that this can be proved.
statement: On the interior of a spectral band, choose the Bloch branch with positive conserved current \(j=\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\psi^{\prime})\). Its phase satisfies \(p^{\prime}(E)=(2j)^{-1}\int_{x_0}^{x_0+T}|\psi|^2dx>0\). The reciprocal multiplier travels in the opposite angular direction. Thus the two roots cannot both be said to rotate in the same direction without a branch convention.
reconstruction: The specific monotonicity statement and current orientation are a reconstruction of the terse sentence.
fate: The discriminant and phase theory is classical; compare \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The phase derivative identity is obtained by differentiating the differential equation and its Floquet boundary condition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The physical trapping and exponential-decay shorthand
notes: The physical sketch contrasts transmission with trapping; a nearby fragment says that forbidden zones decay exponentially.
statement: In an open gap the two Bloch solutions grow and decay exponentially in opposite spatial directions; neither is a nonzero solution decaying at both infinities for the unperturbed periodic operator. If the fragment instead refers to the widths of high-energy gaps, an exponential estimate needs regularity assumptions beyond the written periodicity. The notes do not identify which decay is intended.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} supplies the first Floquet interpretation. No exact assertion about gap-width asymptotics or a localized particle state can be recovered from this fragment.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: Extrema of the discriminant and the sign of the lower bound
notes: The graph is said to have infinitely many maxima and minima, with both written as \(\ge1\).
statement: For a real periodic scalar Schrödinger operator, real critical points of the discriminant lie outside open band interiors. Its successive maxima satisfy \(\tau\ge1\) and minima satisfy \(\tau\le-1\), allowing equality at closed gaps. High-energy asymptotics yield infinitely many such extrema.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives the standard discriminant picture. The source drawing itself puts minima below \(-1\), confirming that the verbal inequality needs a sign or absolute value.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Open band edges, closed gaps and monodromy Jordan form
notes: One selects simple roots of \(\tau(E)=\pm1\) for band endpoints; these give Jordan cells, while a diagonal matrix is degenerate.
statement: At an endpoint of an open gap, \(\tau^2-1\) has a simple zero and monodromy has a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue \(+1\) or \(-1\). At a closed gap, the zero is double and \(M=\pm I\). Removing these double points gives the finite-gap curve. This concerns a real self-adjoint scalar periodic equation.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} explains the scalar Floquet alternative. The notebook\textquotesingle s reference to Gelfand--Lidskii (1955) is broader; no exact claim from that paper is substituted here.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The normalization-independent Riccati variable
notes: The logarithmic derivative is \(\chi=-i\Psi^{\prime}/\Psi\); it does not depend on \(x_0\), is periodic in \(x\), and satisfies a Riccati equation.
statement: On a fixed Bloch branch, away from zeros of \(\Psi\), multiplication by an \(x\)-independent normalization cancels in \(\chi\). Floquet periodicity gives \(\chi(x+T,E)=\chi(x,E)\), and substitution in \(L\Psi=E\Psi\) gives \(-i\chi_x+\chi^2+u-E=0\). The identities extend meromorphically across the divisor.
fate: The Riccati construction and its role in conserved densities are recalled in \citet[\S2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}; the substitution itself is elementary.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Amplitude, phase and the real part of the Riccati variable
notes: The formulas are \(\chi_I=\tfrac12\chi_{R,x}/\chi_R\), \(|\Psi|^2=\chi_R(x_0)/\chi_R(x)\), and \(p=\int_0^T\chi_Rdx\) up to a phase integer.
statement: For real \(E\) in a band interior, choose a branch with nonzero current. Separating the Riccati equation yields \(\chi_I=\tfrac12(\log|\chi_R|)_x\). Consequently \[\Psi(x)=\sqrt{\frac{\chi_R(x_0)}{\chi_R(x)}}\exp\!\left(i\int_{x_0}^x\chi_R(s)ds\right).\] The positive amplitude ratio is periodic, so \(p=\int_{x_0}^{x_0+T}\chi_Rdx\pmod{2\pi}\).
reconstruction: The relation between real and imaginary parts applies on real bands, not literally to arbitrary complex \(E\).
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} uses the amplitude-phase factorization. The source\textquotesingle s overwritten factor before \(\pi n\) is not recoverable; the multiplier fixes the modulus \(2\pi\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The high-energy Riccati expansion and local differential polynomials
notes: An expansion \(\chi\sim k+\sum_{m\ge1}\chi_m(x)/(2k)^m\), \(k=\sqrt E\), is obtained from the Riccati equation; the real part contains odd-index terms.
statement: For a smooth potential, the formal recursion is \(\chi_1=-u\), \(\chi_{m+1}=i\partial_x\chi_m-\sum_{a+b=m}\chi_a\chi_b\). Thus \(\chi_2=-iu_x\) and \(\chi_3=u_{xx}-u^2\). Odd coefficients are real and even coefficients imaginary for real \(u\). The corresponding analytic high-energy expansion is asymptotic in suitable complex sectors; convergence of the infinite series is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} records the recursion framework underlying the higher KdV integrals. The displayed first coefficients are checked directly from the notebook\textquotesingle s convention.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The monodromy formula and the missing subtraction
notes: Formula (1) has \(\sqrt{1-\tau^2}/\alpha_{21}\) plus \((i/2)\alpha_{11}\alpha_{22}/\alpha_{21}\), with no visible operator between the two diagonal entries.
statement: With the row convention \(c(x+T)=a_{11}c(x)+a_{12}s(x)\), \(s(x+T)=a_{21}c(x)+a_{22}s(x)\), and multiplier \(\mu=\tau+i\sqrt{1-\tau^2}\), one has \[\chi(x_0,E)=\frac{\sqrt{1-\tau^2}}{a_{21}}+\frac i2\frac{a_{11}-a_{22}}{a_{21}}.\] Indeed \(\Psi=c+i\chi s\) gives \(\mu=a_{11}+i\chi a_{21}\). The formula is meromorphic where the denominator vanishes.
fate: This is direct two-dimensional eigenvector algebra consistent with \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The required subtraction is a mathematical reconstruction, not a confidently identified hidden stroke.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The Wronskian normalization at the base point
notes: The line reads \(\{c,\Psi\}|_{x_0}=i\Psi^{\prime}(x_0)=i\chi(x_0)\), with an overwritten middle symbol.
statement: Using \(W(c,\Psi)=c\Psi^{\prime}-c^{\prime}\Psi\), \(c(x_0)=1,c^{\prime}(x_0)=0,\Psi(x_0)=1\), the correct identity is \(W(c,\Psi)=\Psi^{\prime}(x_0)=i\chi(x_0)\). The extra factor \(i\) before \(\Psi^{\prime}\) is inconsistent with these definitions.
reconstruction: The overwritten glyph remains palaeographically uncertain; only the mathematical identity is fixed.
fate: The check uses the preceding normalization and Wronskian constancy, the same standard construction as \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Cancelling the closed-gap entire factor
notes: The notes divide \(a_{21}\) by \(\sqrt{(1-\tau^2)/R}\), asserting that the quotient is entire.
statement: In the finite-gap real periodic case, the zeros of \(1-\tau^2\) not included in \(R\) are precisely the closed-gap double zeros. Therefore \((1-\tau^2)/R\) has an entire square root \(H(E)\), up to sign, and \(a_{21}\) vanishes at its zeros. Division removes those simple zeros and gives an entire function \(P=a_{21}/H\).
reconstruction: The multiplicities and removability are needed; a bare quotient of two entire functions need not be entire.
fate: The finite-gap reduction is developed in \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} and announced in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Why the reduced entire function is a polynomial
notes: From \(\chi_R\sim k\) and the leading power of \(\sqrt R\), the notes conclude that the reduced function is a polynomial in \(E\).
statement: The conclusion requires complex growth control in addition to removability. If an entire \(P\) satisfies a global bound \(|P(E)|\le C(1+|E|)^N\), Cauchy estimates give \(\deg P\le N\); the leading normalization then gives degree \(N\). Asymptotics on the positive real axis alone do not imply this: \(E^N+e^{-E}\) has the same leading behaviour there and is not a polynomial.
reconstruction: The global polynomial bound is a sufficient editorial reconstruction, not a hypothesis visibly stated in the notes or a proof that the notes supplied it.
fate: The established finite-gap polynomial conclusion is in \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The notebook omits the sectorial estimates and their global complex-analytic use; the elementary implication above audits that gap in the sketch.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The polynomial representation of the Riccati variable
notes: The final formulas are \(\chi_R=\sqrt R/P\), \(P=\prod(E-\gamma_i(x))\), and \(\chi=(\sqrt R-iP_x/2)/P\).
statement: For the nonsingular finite-gap construction, the monic degree-\(N\) divisor polynomial \(P(E,x)\) gives \[\chi=\frac{\sqrt{R(E)}-\frac i2P_x(E,x)}{P(E,x)}.\] Compatibility with the Schrödinger equation is the identity \[R=(E-u)P^2+\tfrac12PP_{xx}-\tfrac14P_x^2,\] and its derivative yields \(P_{xxx}-4(u-E)P_x-2u_xP=0\). The notation \(\chi_R\) away from real bands means analytic continuation, not the nonholomorphic operation of taking a real part.
fate: \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} and \citet[Ch.~II]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} supply the classical finite-gap formula. The companion\textquotesingle s separate compatibility audit expands the identity directly.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The leading power of the spectral square root
notes: The line gives \(\sqrt{R(E)}\sim E^N\), while the next numerator is \(kE^N\).
statement: Since \(R\) is monic of degree \(2N+1\), one has \(\sqrt{R(E)}\sim E^{N+1/2}=kE^N\) on a chosen sectorial square-root branch. Division by a monic degree-\(N\) polynomial then gives \(\chi_R\sim k\).
fate: The correction follows from the degree of the polynomial written in the notes and agrees with \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Conserved Riccati integrals and the stationary variational equation
notes:
The integrals \(I_n[u]=\int_0^T\chi_{2n+3}(x)dx\) are introduced, followed by
\[\frac{\delta}{\delta u}\Bigl(\sum c_nI_n\Bigr)=d.\]
statement: For smooth periodic \(u\), the odd Riccati densities integrate to local conserved functionals of the KdV hierarchy, up to normalization and total derivatives. A stationary linear combination of flows \(u_t=\partial_x\delta(\sum c_nI_n)/\delta u\) satisfies \(\delta(\sum c_nI_n)/\delta u=d\), where the sum is finite and \(d\) is a spatial constant.
fate: \citet[\S2, equations (6)--(8), Theorem~2.1]{novikov1974periodic} publishes the stationary variational construction and its complete integrability in July 1974, before the September talk. \citet[\S2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} recalls and attributes this result; its new converse is treated separately in item 1974-340.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The derivative order of the Riccati densities
notes: The odd coefficient is written \(\chi_{2n+1}=Q(u,u^{\prime},\ldots,u^{(n-1)})\).
statement: Before integrating by parts, \(\chi_{2n+1}\) generally contains derivatives through order \(2n\). Its leading linear term is \((-1)^{n+1}u^{(2n)}\); already \(\chi_3=u_{xx}-u^2\) contradicts the written order. Integrated densities may be replaced by lower-order representatives modulo total derivatives, but that is a different statement.
fate: The recursion in item 1974-340.16 verifies the correction directly; compare the density construction of \citet[\S2]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}. The doubtful exponent is retained in the source transcription and emended only mathematically.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The energy weak formulation of a quasilinear system
notes: The weak equation sums \(a_{ij}^{hk}(x,u)D_i u^hD_j\varphi^k\); the following strong equation instead writes \(D_i u^k\) inside the sum over \(h\).
statement: For \(u\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb R^N)\), bounded coefficients and compactly supported smooth tests, the weak system is \[\sum_{i,j,h,k}\int_\Omega a_{ij}^{hk}(x,u)D_i u^hD_j\varphi^k\,dx=0.\] It is equivalent to \(\sum_{i,j,h}D_j(a_{ij}^{hk}(x,u)D_i u^h)=0\) in distributions for each \(k\). Here \(D_i=\partial/\partial x_i\), and the unknown argument lies in \(\mathbb R^N\).
fate: \citet[\S3.2, equation (3.5)]{mingione2006regularity} uses the same energy-system formulation. The repeated component index in the strong equation is a correctable mismatch with the preceding weak form.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Strong ellipticity and the distinction from coefficient smoothness
notes: The displayed quadratic form is bounded below by \(|\xi|^2\).
statement: The relevant system assumption is \(\sum a_{ij}^{hk}(x,v)\xi_i^h\xi_j^k\ge\nu|\xi|^2\), for all real \(N\times n\) matrices \(\xi\), together with a uniform upper bound \(|a(x,v)|\le\Lambda\). Analyticity of \(a\) as a function of \(v\) does not imply continuity of the composite \(a(x,u(x))\) if \(u\) is discontinuous.
reconstruction: The uniform upper bound, omitted in the displayed inequality, is part of the standard energy estimates.
fate: \citet[\S3.2]{mingione2006regularity} explains exactly this mechanism in the Giusti--Miranda example. Ellipticity is an algebraic lower bound, not an automatic smoothness conclusion for systems.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The Sobolev energy space and zero trace
notes: The notes define \(W^{1,2}\) by square-integrable function and gradient and describe \(W^{1,2}_0\) as zero boundary values.
statement: For an open set \(\Omega\), \(W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R^N)\) consists of functions with all first weak derivatives in \(L^2\). The space \(W_0^{1,2}\) is the closure of \(C_c^\infty\) in that norm. On a Lipschitz domain this is precisely the subspace with zero Sobolev trace.
fate: This is the standard framework explicitly used in \citet[\S3]{mingione2006regularity}. The trace formulation needs a regular boundary, whereas the closure definition does not.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Scalar or two-dimensional regularity in the energy class
notes: The cases \(N=1\) or \(n\le2\) are called regular, but the line writes \(W^{1,1}\); smooth coefficients are then said to give smooth solutions.
statement: For the homogeneous second-order divergence systems under boundedness and uniform strong ellipticity, scalar energy weak solutions are locally Hölder continuous; in two dimensions the same Hölder conclusion holds for systems, using higher integrability and Sobolev embedding. The relevant class is \(W^{1,2}\). For smooth dependence on \((x,u)\), elliptic bootstrap applies on a region where the solution is already regular; it does not smooth every vectorial weak solution in higher dimensions.
fate: \citet[\S3.1 and Theorem~4.1]{mingione2006regularity} explains the two-dimensional energy argument; \citet[pp.~28--29]{johnstara1990regularity} states the scalar and two-variable alternatives. These are classical pre-talk facts.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The Giusti coefficient tensor and the singular radial solution
notes: For \(n=N\ge3\), the first factor has coefficient \(1/(n-2)\), the second \(4/(n-2)\), and \(u(x)=x/|x|\) is claimed to solve the homogeneous system.
statement: For \(A_{ij}^{hk}(v)=\delta_{ij}\delta_{hk}+(\delta_{jk}+\alpha v_jv_k/(1+|v|^2))(\delta_{ih}+\beta v_iv_h/(1+|v|^2))\), substitution gives \[\sum_{i,j,h}\partial_j(A_{ij}^{hk}(u)\partial_i u^h)=(n-1)\left(\frac{\alpha(n-2)}2-2\right)\frac{x_k}{|x|^3}.\] Thus the written \(\alpha=1/(n-2)\) fails away from the origin. Taking \(\alpha=\beta=4/(n-2)\) gives analytic bounded uniformly elliptic coefficients and a discontinuous weak solution \(u\in W^{1,2}(B_1;\mathbb R^n)\), with trace \(u=x\).
reconstruction: The replacement of the first 1 by 4 is a mathematically forced reconstruction within this tensor ansatz and agrees with the later published formula. It is not a claim to have read a hidden 4 in the scan.
fate: \citet[equation (3.3)]{mingione2006regularity} prints both factors with \(4/(n-2)\), attributing the construction to Giusti--Miranda (1968). The original paper was not retrieved. The exact contraction, residual, ellipticity and weak extension at zero are proved in this companion\textquotesingle s audit.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected energy-class example is verified; the literal tensor is incompatible with the stated solution.

title: A three-variable, two-component counterexample without a specified system
notes: The notes assert an example with \(n=3,N=2\), giving neither its coefficient formula nor a reference.
statement: The exact claim depends on whether coefficients are merely measurable in \(x\), analytic in \((x,u)\), or whether lower-order quadratic gradient terms are allowed. The preceding radial map has \(N=n\) and does not itself establish the two-component case.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.1]{frehse2007irregular} gives a later two-real-component example in dimension three through a complex scalar equation with measurable spatial coefficients (preprint July 2007). Its discussion of the 1973 example involves a different semilinear equation. These are partial contextual matches, not verification of the same analytic homogeneous class intended here.
present_status: As of November 2026, counterexamples in neighbouring classes are known, but the precise 1974 assertion and its coefficient class have not been identified.

title: The unverified uniqueness assertion for singular Dirichlet data
notes: For \(|x|=1\), \(u_i=x_i\), the notes write \(\exists!\) solution and say that it is nonregular.
statement: The corrected tensor supplies at least one singular \(W^{1,2}\) solution with trace \(x\). Uniqueness among all weak solutions does not follow from positive definiteness of \(A(u)\), because the coefficient depends on the unknown. No monotonicity of the full nonlinear operator, admissible subclass or uniqueness proof is recorded.
fate: \citet[\S3.2]{mingione2006regularity} distinguishes a variational construction from the homogeneous system. The source matching and the companion\textquotesingle s residual proof establish existence only; no exact uniqueness theorem was verified.
present_status: As of November 2026, existence is verified for the reconstructed system; the uniqueness claim in the notebook remains unverified and is not used.

title: A relatively closed singular set of dimension strictly below n minus two
notes: For continuous coefficients, the regular set \(\Omega_0\) is open, its complement \(K\) is relatively closed, \(\mathcal H^{n-2}(K)=0\), and \(\dim K<n-2\).
statement: For \(n\ge3\), let \(u\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb R^N)\) solve \(\operatorname{div}(A(x,u)Du)=0\), with bounded uniformly strongly elliptic coefficients uniformly continuous in \((x,v)\). There is an open regular set \(\Omega_u\) where \(u\) is locally Hölder of every exponent below one, and \(\dim_H(\Omega\setminus\Omega_u)<n-2\). In particular \(\mathcal H^{n-2}(K)=0\). The strict dimension statement uses more than the latter zero-measure statement alone.
reconstruction: Uniform bounds, uniform continuity, the energy class and the meaning of regularity are restored. The original source merely says continuous coefficients.
fate: \citet[\S1.1, equations (1.1)--(1.2)]{defilippismingionenowak2026partial} restates this precise classical local theorem and attributes its foundation to Giusti--Miranda and Morrey (1968). The 2025 preprint, revised July 2026, is used to verify the hypotheses and bound, not to date the original result to 2026.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: The compressed higher-order partial-regularity bound
notes: For order \(m>2\), the notes write \(\dim K\le n-2\).
statement: The notebook does not specify whether \(m\) is the differential order or half-order, which derivatives are required to be regular, or the coefficient dependence and growth. Therefore the displayed dimension bound is not a complete theorem.
fate: \citet[Theorems 1--2]{giusti1969partial} treats arbitrary-order quasilinear systems before the talk (received 1968; published 1969), but the opened scan did not permit a reliable exact-hypothesis comparison with this one-line bound. No specific modern higher-order theorem is substituted.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source does not determine a sufficiently precise claim for an open-problem status.

title: Variational problems with nonregular minimizers
notes: The notes ask whether there are variational problems with nonregular solutions.
statement: In the broad class of vector-valued uniformly elliptic variational integrals \(\int F(x,u,Du)\), are there energy-class minimizing maps that are not continuous? Yes: analytic dependence of the quadratic coefficient tensor on \(u\) is compatible with a discontinuous local minimizer in sufficiently large dimensions. The question does not impose autonomous dependence only on \(Du\).
reconstruction: “Solutions” is read as minimizers, the stronger variational interpretation; the distinction from merely stationary points is explicit.
fate: \citet[\S3.2, equations (3.3)--(3.4)]{mingione2006regularity} explicitly records the Giusti--Miranda 1968 variational example. Thus the broad question was already answered before this talk. Stronger later autonomous examples are not treated as an answer to an unstated restriction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated reconstruction is a standard established result.

title: Gelfand’s proposed analogue of resolution of singularities
notes: Gelfand asks for an analogue of Hironaka resolution of singularities for elliptic equations.
statement: No class of equations, admissible modification, transformed unknown, or required regularity after modification is specified. Resolving analytic zero sets, desingularizing coefficients and resolving singular weak solutions are distinct possible problems. The analogy alone does not select a definite conjecture.
fate: The partial-regularity and counterexample literature above concerns the size and occurrence of singular sets, not a universal resolution operation. Searches for an exact publication of this elliptic-resolution programme did not identify one; Hironaka\textquotesingle s algebraic theorem cannot be transferred without a specified analytic statement.
present_status: As of November 2026, the recorded programme remains insufficiently specified for a mathematical open-problem status or a claimed new solution.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Analytic expressions in combinatorial characteristic-class calculations
notes: \ru{О раб. Габриэлова, И. Гельфанда и Лосика по комбинаторной топологии}; \ru{Интересно сделать аналитически}. The logarithmic integrals are said to occur in a finite combinatorial problem.
statement: The identifiable programme is to express characteristic classes of triangulated smooth manifolds by local combinatorial data, with analytic functions entering the formula. The page does not specify a triangulation, cochain, normalization, or the particular class, and hence does not state a theorem that can be reconstructed uniquely.
fate: \citet[pp.~103--115]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation} and \citet[pp.~186--202]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975calculus} are the directly attributable publications in 1975 (received 2 December 1974 and 31 March 1975). Their subject and authors match; the notebook does not support an exact theorem match.
present_status: As of November 2026, the publication family is identified. The particular finite combinatorial problem invoked by this paragraph remains unspecified; no new open problem is inferred.

title: The logarithmic integral and the Rogers dilogarithm
notes: The notes write \(\int_{1-x}^{x}\{\log|t|/(1-t)+\log|1-t|/t\}\,dt\), saying it cannot be evaluated in elementary functions.
statement: For \(0<x<1\), set \(L(x)=\operatorname{Li}_2(x)+\tfrac12\log x\log(1-x)\). Then the displayed integral equals \(-2[L(x)-L(1-x)]\). This is a dilogarithmic antiderivative, not an assertion that every individual special value is non-elementary.
reconstruction: The domain and the explicit identification with the real Rogers dilogarithm are editorial; the notebook gives only the integral.
fate: This is classical dilogarithm calculus, documented with the derivative and reflection formula in \citet[Chapter II, \S1.A, pp.~23--24]{zagier2007dilogarithm}. The modern reference does not date the formula to 2007.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The sign of the Basel integral
notes: The scan explicitly has \(\int_0^1\log|1-t|\,dt/t=+\pi^2/6\), followed by a positive power-series sum.
statement: The convergent improper integral is \(\int_0^1\log(1-t)\,dt/t=-\zeta(2)=-\pi^2/6\). Termwise integration of \(-\log(1-t)=\sum_{n\ge1}t^n/n\) is justified by monotone convergence.
fate: The corrected identity is classical; see \citet[Eqs.~25.12.1--2]{nist2026polylogarithms}. The error is already in the handwriting, not introduced by the English translation.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: A correct golden-ratio dilogarithm evaluation
notes: For \(a=\sqrt5-2\), the notes give \(\int_{-a}^a\{\log|t|/(1-t)+\log|1-t|/t\}\,dt=-\pi^2/6\), adding \ru{из топологических соображений}.
statement: The improper integral through \(t=0\) exists and the stated value is correct. It follows from the reflection and five-term equations for the real Rogers dilogarithm; the notebook supplies no topological argument.
fate: The analytic identity reduces to classical functional equations, as in \citet[Chapter II, \S1.A]{zagier2007dilogarithm}. A complete verification and two independent numerical checks are supplied in the verification appendix. This establishes the reading without attributing our proof to the speaker.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Periodic Hill operator and bounded Bloch solutions
notes: \(-y^{\prime\prime}+u(x)y=Ey\); the written periodicity is \(u(x+T)=u(y)\). The spectrum is described as the energies having bounded eigenfunctions.
statement: For real \(T\)-periodic \(u\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\), let \(L=-d^2/dx^2+u\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R)\), domain \(H^2\). Its spectrum consists precisely of real energies with a nonzero bounded solution of \(Ly=Ey\). These are generalized eigenfunctions, generally not \(L^2(\mathbb R)\) eigenvectors.
reconstruction: Real smooth periodic potential and operator domain are stated explicitly; the displayed u(y) is emended to u(x).
fate: Classical Floquet theory, recapitulated in \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; compare earlier occurrence 1973-326.2 and 1973-326.8.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Characterizing finite-gap potentials by stationary KdV
notes: \ru{Проблема Новикова: когда есть конечн. число запрещ. зон?} The answer is written as a nonlinear ordinary differential equation \(K(u,u^{\prime},\ldots,u^{(2N+1)})=0\) from the KdV hierarchy.
