statement: A real smooth periodic potential has finitely many open bounded spectral gaps if and only if it is stationary for a nontrivial finite real linear combination of the KdV hierarchy flows (equivalently, its Schr\"odinger operator commutes with an odd-order scalar differential operator). The least nondegenerate order corresponds to the number of open gaps; a higher stationary equation need not have all its gaps open.
reconstruction: The phrase KdV equations is interpreted as stationary finite linear combinations, not the evolutionary PDE \(u_t=6uu_x-u_{xxx}\). Publication within 1974 is clear; precise issue-day priority relative to 23 September is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}, received 18 February 1974 and published July 1974, proves stationary KdV implies finite-gap. The converse is explicit in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974. The full account is \citet[Chapter 2, \S2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Class A refers to that converse and full characterization, not to the already published forward implication. Earlier occurrences include 1973-326.15 and 1974-340.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Monodromy and its discriminant
notes: The normalized \(c,s\) solutions, the translation matrix \(\widehat T=(\alpha_{ij})\), \(\det\widehat T=1\), and \(\lambda^2-2\tau\lambda+1=0\) with \(2\tau=\alpha_{11}+\alpha_{22}\) are written.
statement: Normalize \(c(x_0)=s^{\prime}(x_0)=1\), \(c^{\prime}(x_0)=s(x_0)=0\). The period map on the two-dimensional solution space has determinant one by the constant Wronskian. Its eigenvalues are \(\tau(E)\pm\sqrt{\tau(E)^2-1}\); every matrix entry and \(\tau\) is entire in \(E\).
fate: Classical monodromy construction; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.1)--(2.1.8)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Earlier occurrence: 1973-326.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Allowed and forbidden intervals from the discriminant
notes: An allowed energy has a Bloch function with \(|\lambda|=1\); \(\tau^2\le1\) is allowed and \(\tau^2>1\) forbidden. Two drawings correct the oscillation of the discriminant.
statement: For the real periodic problem, \(\sigma(L)=\{E\in\mathbb R:|\tau(E)|\le1\}\). Periodic and antiperiodic eigenvalues give band endpoints. Critical points of the discriminant above the spectral bottom lie in the closures of spectral gaps, and extrema alternate at levels at least1 and at most−1 respectively. A closed gap means a tangency at \(+1\) or \(-1\), not that the entire discriminant becomes constant.
fate: Classical Hill spectral theory; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The notebook\textquotesingle s later \(\max\) and \(\min\) both equal 1 is a sign omission, visible after the corrected sketch.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Closed gaps have scalar monodromy
notes: If \(\tau^2(E)=1\) has a multiple root, the notes infer \(\alpha_{12}=\alpha_{21}=0\), distinguishing a Jordan band edge from a diagonal one.
statement: For a real periodic Hill operator, a double periodic or antiperiodic eigenvalue has two independent periodic or antiperiodic solutions, so its monodromy is \(+I\) or \(-I\). Thus both off-diagonal entries vanish in every basis; a simple edge generally has a nontrivial Jordan block. This uses the differential equation and self-adjoint boundary problem, not the characteristic polynomial of an arbitrary matrix alone.
fate: Classical closed-gap criterion; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; earlier 1973-326.12.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Removing double branch points from the spectral curve
notes: There are \(2N+1\) simple finite roots \(E_j\) of \(\tau^2-1\), the other roots are double; a radical involving \((\tau^2-1)/\prod(E-E_j)\) is called single-valued.
statement: If the real periodic spectrum has exactly \(N\) open bounded gaps and distinct endpoints \(E_1<\cdots<E_{2N+1}\), then \((\tau^2(E)-1)/\prod_j(E-E_j)\) is entire with only even-order zeros, hence has an entire square root. The remaining two-sheeted compact curve is \(w^2=\prod_j(E-E_j)\), of genus \(N\).
reconstruction: The quotient under one square root is the mathematical reading, not a claim that the scan is unambiguous.
fate: The finite-gap reduction is in \citet[Chapter 2, \S\S1--2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The radical must include the quotient; the handwritten overbar alone does not decide its full scope. The spectral-curve and divisor statements are explicitly announced in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974; this is a firmer contemporary match than the later survey alone.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The Riccati logarithmic derivative
notes: \(\chi=-i\Psi^{\prime}/\Psi\); it is independent of the normalizing point \(x_0\), periodic in \(x\), and satisfies \(-i\chi^{\prime}+\chi^2+u-E=0\).
statement: For a chosen nonzero Bloch solution, away from its zeros, the logarithmic derivative is independent of scalar normalization, is \(T\)-periodic, and obeys that Riccati equation. Branch choice in spectral parameter remains; independence of \(x_0\) means that the same Bloch line is selected.
fate: Classical Riccati substitution, written in precisely this convention in \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.10)--(2.1.12)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Amplitude and phase of a Bloch solution
notes:
In an allowed band the notes write
\[\begin{aligned}
\chi_I&=\chi_R^{\prime}/(2\chi_R),\\
\Psi&=\sqrt{\chi_R(x_0,E)/\chi_R(x,E)}
       \exp\Bigl(i\int_{x_0}^x\chi_R\Bigr),\\
|\Psi|^2&=\chi_R(x_0,E)/\chi_R(x,E).
\end{aligned}\]
statement: For real \(u,E\) with \(E\) inside an open spectral band, choose a nonreal Bloch line and its conjugate, with nonzero Wronskian. Then \(a=\operatorname{Re}\chi\) never vanishes, \(\operatorname{Im}\chi=a^{\prime}/(2a)\), and the displayed normalized amplitude-phase formula holds with a continuous square root equal to 1 at \(x=x_0\). It need not hold at a band endpoint without a limiting interpretation.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.12)--(2.1.14)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives these formulas.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Formal high-energy densities and parity
notes: For \(E=k^2\), \(\chi\sim k+\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_n/(2k)^n\); the coefficients are differential polynomials in \(u\). The real part contains only odd inverse powers.
statement: For smooth real \(u\), the formal Riccati solution with leading term \(k\) is obtained recursively. In this convention \(\chi_1=-u\), \(\chi_2=-iu^{\prime}\), \(\chi_3=u^{\prime\prime}-u^2\). Odd coefficients are real and even coefficients imaginary; even terms are total derivatives and integrate to zero over a period. A formal expansion is not a claim of convergence.
reconstruction: The first coefficients and formal-versus-convergent distinction are supplied editorially. Signs follow the notebook\textquotesingle s chi=-i psi prime/psi convention.
fate: \citet[Chapter 1, \S1 and Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.18)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; compare 1973-326.19.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Quasimomentum as a generating function
notes: \(\lambda=e^{ip(E)}\), \(p(E)=\int_{x_0}^{x_0+T}\chi_R(x,E)\,dx+2\pi n\); the Euler equations for its expansion are called KdV equations.
statement: For a selected Bloch branch, \(p\) is defined modulo \(2\pi\). Its high-energy expansion yields integrals of local differential polynomials invariant under isospectral KdV flows. Hamiltonian evolution generated by these integrals gives the KdV hierarchy; critical points of finite linear combinations give stationary equations. The Euler--Lagrange equation alone is not the evolutionary KdV equation.
reconstruction: The distinction between variational critical-point equations and Hamiltonian time evolution repairs an abbreviated phrase.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.15) and \S2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The stationary hierarchy mechanism is already in \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}. The cited Novikov article appeared inJuly 1974, before the23 September catalogue date; this occurrence is therefore expository.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Variational derivative of quasimomentum
notes: \(\delta p(E)/\delta u(x)=-1/(2\chi_R(x,E))\).
statement: For real smooth periodic \(u\), a spectral parameter in a band interior, and a fixed local branch of quasimomentum, its first variation under periodic \(v\) is \(D p(u)[v]=-\tfrac12\int_0^T v(x)/\chi_R(x,E)\,dx\). The local choice removes the additive \(2\pi\) ambiguity; analytic continuation requires consistent sheet choice.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.17)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives the negative-sign formula. The identity is already announced in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974, but the opened English version prints a positive sign. With the present convention \(p(E;u_0)=T\sqrt{E-u_0}\) for constant potential, direct differentiation gives \(\delta p/\delta u(x)=-1/(2\sqrt{E-u_0})\), so the negative sign is forced. The notebook agrees with this check.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Expressing the logarithmic derivative through monodromy
notes: \(\chi=\sqrt{1-\tau^2}/\alpha_{21}+\tfrac i2(\alpha_{11}-\alpha_{22})/\alpha_{21}\).
statement: Use the coefficient-basis convention \(T=\begin{pmatrix}c(T)&c^{\prime}(T)\\s(T)&s^{\prime}(T)\end{pmatrix}\), so \(\alpha_{21}=s(T)\). Solving the Bloch eigenvector equation gives the displayed expression, with the sign of the square root selecting the multiplier. Where \(s(T)=0\), interpret it meromorphically or use the other chart.
reconstruction: The manuscript leaves its matrix-entry convention implicit. The transposed coefficient convention is selected so the written alpha21 formula is valid.
fate: The two basis conventions are distinguished in \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.19)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Changing to the usual fundamental-state matrix interchanges the off-diagonal indices.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The finite-gap polynomial divisor representation
notes: \(R(E)=\prod_{j=1}^{2N+1}(E-E_j)\), \(P(E,x)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(E-\gamma_j(x))\), \(\chi=\sqrt R/P-\tfrac i2P_x/P\).
statement: For a nonsingular real finite-gap Schr\"odinger potential with \(N\) open gaps, choose the branch of \(\sqrt R\) behaving as \(E^{N+1/2}\), and the monic degree-\(N\) divisor polynomial \(P\). Its zeros and poles must satisfy the Schr\"odinger compatibility identity, so an arbitrary pair of polynomials does not suffice.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S\S2--3]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; the relation between stationary operators and the spectral polynomial appears in \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}. title: Bloch function on the hyperelliptic curve
notes: Dubrovin states that \(\Psi(x,x_0,E)\) is single-valued on \(\Gamma_N\), meromorphic away from infinity, with \(N\) zeros above \(\gamma_i(x)\) and \(N\) poles above \(\gamma_i(x_0)\).
statement: For nonsingular finite-gap spectral data with a nonspecial divisor of degree \(N\), the normalized Baker--Akhiezer function is single-valued and meromorphic on the curve minus its point at infinity; its polar divisor is bounded by the initial divisor and its zero divisor by the moving divisor, with \(N\) points counting multiplicity before cancellation. At \(x=x_0\) the function is 1, so coincident zero and pole divisors cancel. At infinity it has the prescribed exponential singularity.
reconstruction: Multiplicity, divisor cancellation, nonspeciality and the exponential behavior at infinity are made explicit; the literal count fails at the normalization point.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, p.~77 and \S3]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} supplies the divisor description and theta-function inverse construction. title: Unordered configurations and the electric-field map
notes: \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\) consists of unordered subsets of cardinality \(k\). Unit charges define \(f_S\), with each particle sent to infinity and infinity sent to zero, and the resulting sphere map has degree \(k\).
statement: For \(n>1\), choose a decaying radial field with a pole of fixed local degree at each point of a configuration. Its one-point compactification gives a continuous map \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\to\Omega^n_k S^n\), where the source sphere is based at infinity and the target at zero. Orient the target so that each positive pole contributes degree \(+1\); then the total degree is \(k\).
reconstruction: The based mapping space, n>1 for the electrostatic description, and orientation convention are made explicit. Scanning gives the corresponding construction also in dimension 1.
fate: The construction is already explicit in \citet[\S1, p.~213]{segal1973configuration}, published in 1973. Its description agrees unusually closely with the notebook.

pages: P000569, homology display; P000570, stable limit
title: Stable homology approximation and group completion
notes: \(H_i(C_k(\mathbb R^n))\cong H_i(\mathrm{Map}_k(S^n,S^n))\) for \(i\ll k\). The right-hand side is homotopically independent of \(k\), while configurations stabilize by adding particles.

title: Configuration spaces as classifying spaces
notes: Fuchs says that \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\) gives different classifying spaces, without naming the groups or a limiting dimension.
statement: Two standard instances make the remark precise: \(C_k(\mathbb R^2)\) is a classifying space for the braid group, and \(C_k(\mathbb R^\infty)\) is a classifying space for \(\Sigma_k\). title: The topology of signed configurations
notes: Finite subsets carry charges of either sign; opposite charges disappear when they meet. Components are indexed by the total charge \(k\in\mathbb Z\).
statement: Let \(C(M)=\coprod_{r\ge0}C_r(M)\). Form \(C^{\pm}(M)\) from \(C(M)\times C(M)\) by cancelling a point common to the positive and negative configurations, with the quotient topology. pages: P000570, crossed comparison and corrected target
title: The correct loop-space target for cancelling particles

title: Scanning a manifold into a section space
notes: \(C_k(M)\to\Gamma_k^{\mathrm{cpt}}(T_M^{\mathrm{comp}})\), with infinity added to each tangent fibre. A finite-range electric field is said to make the construction rigorous.
statement: For a smooth \(n\)-manifold, choose a Riemannian metric and sufficiently small scanning balls. A configuration determines a compactly supported section of the fibrewise one-point compactification \(\dot TM\); outside the scanning support it is the infinity section. title: Stable homology of configurations on manifolds
notes: The manifold scanning map is said to induce a homology isomorphism for \(i\ll k\), without specifying compactness, boundary conditions or a stable range.
statement: For a connected smooth open manifold of dimension at least2 that is the interior of a compact manifold with nonempty boundary, choose an end for stabilization. pages: P000570, failed restriction and boundary quotient
title: Particles disappearing at a boundary
notes: The map \(C(M)\to C(U)\times C(V)\) by restriction is marked discontinuous. For manifolds with boundary, \(\overline C(U)\) identifies configurations agreeing on the interior, so boundary particles disappear.
statement: Cardinality changes when a particle crosses the edge of an open piece, preventing continuity into the disjoint-union configuration topology. pages: P000570, boundary theorem and disk proof
title: Relative configurations and the local disk calculation
notes: For \(U\) with nonempty boundary, \(\overline C(U)\simeq\Gamma(\dot TU)\). For a disk, radially pushing points to the boundary leaves at most one particle, and both sides become \(S^n\).
statement: In the relative scanning model for a compact connected smooth manifold with nonempty boundary, particles are allowed to disappear on all of the boundary and the target consists of sections with unrestricted boundary values. The local model is \(C(D^n,\partial D^n)\simeq D^n/\partial D^n\cong S^n\), while \(\Gamma(\dot TD^n)\simeq\mathrm{Map}(D^n,S^n)\simeq S^n\). pages: P000571, two covering squares and homotopy lifting
title: Local-to-global proof by homotopy pullback
notes: The two restriction squares for \(\overline C\) and sections are compared. Homotopies lift in the restriction maps; equivalences on \(U,V,U\cap V\) then give one on \(U\cup V\).

pages: P000573, Polyakov opening and plaquette sketch
title: Compact-group link variables and plaquette holonomy

title: The Wilson loop as a gauge-invariant correlation

statement: For an oriented closed lattice path \(C\), use the path-ordered product of link variables, replacing a reversed edge by its inverse. Its character is independent of the chosen starting vertex, and its Gibbs expectation is gauge invariant. title: Exact integration in two dimensions
notes: \ru{Плоская зад. решается точно} follows the finite \(N\times N\) lattice definition.
statement: For a simply connected finite planar lattice with open boundary and a central plaquette weight \(w:G\to\mathbb R_{>0}\), a spanning-tree gauge choice reduces the partition integral to independent plaquette integrals. If \(w=\sum_\rho a_\rho\chi_\rho\), the disk amplitude with boundary holonomy \(g\) is \(\sum_\rho d_\rho(a_\rho/d_\rho)^A\chi_\rho(g)\), where \(A\) is the number of plaquettes. Integrating the boundary gives \(Z=a_{\mathrm{triv}}^A\). Periodic boundary identifications impose additional global constraints.
reconstruction: The region, boundary treatment, central weight and character normalization are supplied to make the phrase exactly solvable precise.
fate: The later exact character-expansion formulation is explicitly derived in \citet[Appendix A.1, Eqs.~(A.6)--(A.11)]{hirasawa2020complex}. title: Coupling group-valued spins to a lattice connection
notes: The spin energy \(\sum\chi(g_\tau^{-1}g_{\tau+a_\alpha})\) is followed by \(\sum\chi(g_\tau^{-1}g_{\tau+a_\alpha}B_{\tau,\alpha})+E[B]\).
statement: Group-valued spins with a global symmetry can be coupled to link transport to make the interaction locally gauge invariant. For example, with \(g_x\mapsto g_xh_x^{-1}\) and a reverse transporter \(B_{xy}\mapsto h_yB_{xy}h_x^{-1}\), the factor \(\chi(g_x^{-1}g_yB_{xy})\) is invariant. Equivalently one can use forward links and the conventional \(\chi(g_x^{-1}U_{xy}g_y)\), with the corresponding left action on spins. Mixing these conventions destroys invariance.
reconstruction: The transformation laws are an explicit editorial consistency check. The two energy displays are retained as one gauging construction rather than treated as two unrelated models. In particular the reverse-link convention used to rescue this ordering cannot simultaneously be inserted unchanged into the preceding forward-oriented plaquette formula; one must reverse those links too, or use the conventional forward-link interaction.
fate: Gauge-invariant matter coupling is already present in \citet[\S III.A]{wilson1974confinement}; \citet{baliandrouffeitzykson1974gauge} develops the coupled group-spin model, received 3 June 1974 and published 15 November 1974. title: Euclidean continuation and transfer matrices
notes: Field theory is identified with statistical mechanics in Euclidean \(\mathbb R^n\); the parenthesis says \ru{преобр. Фурье по времени}.
statement: The relevant formal passage from Lorentzian quantum dynamics to Euclidean Gibbs weights is continuation to imaginary time. An ordinary Fourier transform in real time alone does not make the Minkowski action into a positive Euclidean Gibbs energy.

pages: P000573, Sinai partition function; P000574, angular specialization
title: When the Bessel partition function is valid
notes: Sinai writes \(\log Z(\beta,V)=V\log I_0(\beta)\). The next page has \(B=e^{iA}\) and \(E=\sum\cos(\operatorname{curl}A)\).
statement: For the planar \(U(1)\) model with normalized link-angle measure, open boundary, and \(A\) plaquettes, \(Z=I_0(\beta)^A\), where \(I_m(\beta)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}e^{\beta\cos\theta}\cos(m\theta)\,d\theta\). title: Boundary independence of the pressure
notes: \(\lim_{V\to\infty}V^{-1}\log Z(\beta,V)=f(\beta)\) is asserted to be independent of boundary conditions.
statement: For translation-invariant bounded finite-range interactions on compact lattice variables, with normalized product a priori measure, pressure exists along van Hove boxes and is unchanged by boundary conditions whose change affects only a boundary layer of bounded energy per interaction. Indeed boundary choices change \(\log Z\) by at most a constant times the number of boundary interactions, which is \(o(V)\). This is a statement about pressure, not uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs state.
reconstruction: The shape of the limit, bounded finite-range interactions and ordinary boundary perturbations are supplied. Boundary independence alone does not rule out phase coexistence.
fate: The thermodynamic-limit framework precedes the talk; \citet[Theorem 1]{ruelle1967variational} treats lattice pressure for summable interactions in the finite-state setting. The bounded compact-variable formulation here is its standard boundary-estimate extension, not an exact quotation of that theorem. The explicit planar model also has pressure \(\log I_0(\beta)\).

title: Nonanalyticity in the infinite-volume limit
notes: Singularities of \(f(\beta)\) are called phase transitions, accompanied heuristically by a change in typical configurations.
statement: A finite-volume partition integral with bounded energy is entire in complex \(\beta\) and positive for real \(\beta\), so its real logarithm is locally analytic. Thermodynamic singularities can arise only after the infinite-volume limit. Nonanalytic pressure is a thermodynamic phase-transition criterion, while a full classification of Gibbs phases also involves states and order parameters. In the written planar \(U(1)\) model, \(\log I_0(\beta)\) is analytic at every finite real \(\beta\).
fate: The distinction between finite volume and thermodynamic phases is classical; compare \citet[\S I]{wilson1974confinement} and \citet{ruelle1967variational}. The analytic \(I_0\) formula prevents reading this paragraph as a proof of a finite-temperature transition in that particular two-dimensional example.

title: Area and perimeter laws require a specified model
notes: The last two lines say that in one phase the correlation is proportional to area and in another to contour length.
statement: The intended diagnostic is \(-\log|\langle W(C)\rangle|\) growing proportionally to the area enclosed by a large loop or to its perimeter. The expectation itself decays exponentially. Dimension, gauge group, matter content, action, family of loops and limiting regime must be specified before the phrase becomes a theorem. In the planar pure \(U(1)\) model with positive \(\beta\), \(|\langle W(C)\rangle|=(I_1(\beta)/I_0(\beta))^{A(C)}\) for a simple loop, so it has an area law at every finite \(\beta>0\).
fate: \citet[\S II and \S IV]{wilson1974confinement} supplies the area/perimeter criterion and a strong-coupling analysis, but it does not turn the notebook\textquotesingle s unspecified assertion into a universal two-phase theorem. The exact planar conclusion follows from independent plaquette integration; no modern Yang--Mills mass-gap problem is silently substituted.

title: Milnor number as local gradient multiplicity
notes: For an analytic germ without constant or linear terms, \(\mu(f)\) is the multiplicity of the zero solution of \(\partial f/\partial z_i=0\), also described as the maximum number of solutions to \(\partial f/\partial z_i=\varepsilon_i\) for small \(\varepsilon\).
statement: Let \(f\in\mathbb C\{z_1,\ldots,z_n\}\) have an isolated critical point at 0. Then \(\mu(f)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C\{z\}/(f_{z_1},\ldots,f_{z_n})\). For a sufficiently small isolating neighborhood and a sufficiently small generic regular value \(\varepsilon\), the gradient equation has exactly \(\mu(f)\) simple solutions there. Nongeneric perturbations require multiplicities.
reconstruction: Isolation, the local neighborhood, genericity and the distinction between distinct and multiple roots are made explicit.
fate: This local-algebra invariant is part of the established singularity theory preceding the talk. \citet[\S1]{kushnirenko1975newton} fixes the same definition; its use here is expository, while the Newton formula is the new result.

title: The Newton boundary and its alternating volume number
notes: \ru{Задача: вычислить} \(\mu(f)\) from Taylor coefficients. The lower Newton polygon gives \(\nu=2S-a-b+1\); in dimension 3 the formula is \(6V-2(S_{12}+S_{13}+S_{23})+(L_1+L_2+L_3)-1\).
statement: For a convenient germ, meaning its support meets every coordinate axis, take the compact faces of \(\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{supp}f+\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n)\) and the region \(\Gamma_-\) swept out between them and 0. If \(V_j\) is the sum of ordinary \(j\)-dimensional volumes of intersections of \(\Gamma_-\) with coordinate \(j\)-planes and \(V_0=1\), then \(\nu(f)=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^{n-j}j!V_j\). Its cases \(n=2,3\) are exactly the written formulas.

fate: The definition and formulas are in \citet[\S\S2--3]{kushnirenko1975newton}; received 30 September 1974, published 1975. The arbitrary-dimensional expression is also the organizing definition in the full 1976 paper, \citet{kouchnirenko1976polyedres}.

title: Kushnirenko lower bound and equality under nondegeneracy
notes: Both dimension 2 and dimension 3 displays state \(\mu(f)\ge\nu(f)\), with equality under nondegeneracy; the condition holds almost always.
statement: For a convenient holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point, \(\mu(f)\ge\nu(f)\). If for every compact face \(\Delta\) the face polynomial \(f_\Delta\) has no critical point in \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), then equality holds. At a fixed convenient Newton boundary, the exceptional face coefficients lie in a proper algebraic subset, so equality holds generically. Equality for every degenerate germ is not claimed.

The recorded talk establishes circulation by 7 October 1974 and the received date establishes the announcement existed a week earlier.

title: Nondegeneracy of an edge polynomial
notes: The illustration gives \(\beta^2\ne4\alpha\gamma\), and the text calls for the discriminant of each edge to be nonzero, because an edge is essentially a one-variable polynomial.
statement: After removing a monomial and using a primitive lattice coordinate along an edge, its face polynomial becomes a one-variable polynomial. Nonzero roots must be simple. For a quadratic edge polynomial with nonzero endpoint coefficients \(\alpha,\gamma\), this is \(\beta^2-4\alpha\gamma\ne0\). In two variables this test must be applied to every compact edge; in higher dimensions it does not replace the conditions on higher-dimensional faces.
reconstruction: The lattice coordinate, removal of monomial factors and nonzero endpoint coefficients are explicit safeguards against an overbroad discriminant test.
fate: This is the planar face test for the nondegeneracy condition in \citet[\S8]{kushnirenko1975newton}. The precise quadratic discriminant follows by elementary differentiation; it is an explanatory specialization of the new general theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Face nondegeneracy as a finite-codimension ideal
notes: For the cone \(P(\Delta)\) over a face, \(\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[P(\Delta)]/(z_i\partial f_\Delta/\partial z_i)<\infty\) is written.
statement: For a compact face \(\Delta\) disjoint from 0, let \(P(\Delta)=\operatorname{cone}(\Delta)\cap\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n\). In the semigroup ring \(\mathbb C[P(\Delta)]\), require the ideal generated by all logarithmic derivatives \(z_i\partial f_\Delta/\partial z_i\) to have finite vector-space codimension. Requiring this for every face is the algebraic nondegeneracy formulation used in the announcement.
fate: The notation and condition agree exactly with \citet[\S8]{kushnirenko1975newton}. They connect the geometric volume formula to a finite-dimensional quotient; no global polynomial gradient quotient is being taken at this stage.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Cohen--Macaulay semigroup rings in the proof
notes: The proof is said to use commutative algebra and Hochster\textquotesingle s assertion that \(\mathbb C[P(\Delta)]\) is Cohen--Macaulay.
statement: For a finitely generated saturated affine semigroup \(P\), its semigroup algebra over a field is Cohen--Macaulay. The lattice points of the rational polyhedral cone over \(\Delta\) satisfy these hypotheses. This property supplies regular-sequence and Hilbert-series control when the face-gradient ideal has finite codimension.
reconstruction: Saturation and finite generation are essential. An arbitrary ring generated by an arbitrary selection of monomials need not be Cohen--Macaulay.
fate: Hochster\textquotesingle s theorem was published in September 1972, before the lecture: \citet[main theorem, p.~318]{hochster1972invariants}. Its use in this Newton-polyhedron argument is reported by the notebook and developed in \citet{kouchnirenko1976polyedres}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Euler--Jacobi vanishing of the total residue
notes:
For two degree-\(n\) polynomials \(P_n,Q_n\), the notes give
\[\sum_{P_n=Q_n=0}\frac{R_{n-4}(x,y)}
 {\det\bigl(\partial(P_n,Q_n)/\partial(x,y)\bigr)}=0,\]
summing over all \(n^2\) zeros.
statement: Let \(P,Q\in\mathbb C[x,y]\) have degree \(n\ge4\), with leading homogeneous parts having no common nonzero zero, and suppose their \(n^2\) affine intersection points are simple. Then for every polynomial \(R\) of degree at most \(2n-3\), \(\sum_{P(a)=Q(a)=0}R(a)/(P_xQ_y-P_yQ_x)(a)=0\). In particular the notebook\textquotesingle s degree at most \(n-4\) satisfies the theorem.
reconstruction: Transversality, absence of intersections at infinity and \(n\ge4\) are explicit. The stronger \(2n-3\) bound is a literature comparison; \(n-4\) is the legible original reading, not an OCR error.
fate: This is the classical Euler--Jacobi formula, not a newly posed residue problem. \citet[Corollary, p.~237]{khovanskii1978eulerjacobi} states the general degree bound and explicitly treats it as classical, while proving a Newton-polyhedron generalization suggested by Arnold. The 1978 result is a later development of the theme, not evidence that this 1974 formula was new.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The nerve and realization of a category
notes: Objects give vertices, morphisms edges, composable pairs filled triangles, and composable triples tetrahedra. The graph alone does not retain composition.
statement: For a small category \(\mathcal C\), set \(N_k\mathcal C=\operatorname{Fun}([k],\mathcal C)\), with faces given by omission/composition and degeneracies by identities. Its geometric realization is \(B\mathcal C\).
reconstruction: The face and degeneracy maps make the pictured construction precise. A smallness convention is supplied.
fate: \citet[\S2]{segal1968classifying}, received 14 April 1967 and published 1968. Earlier occurrences: 1971-255.2 and 1973-308.11.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: Partially ordered sets as thin categories
notes: The notes identify partially ordered sets with categories having at most one morphism between two objects.
statement: A poset \(P\) defines a category with one arrow \(x\to y\) exactly when \(x\leq y\). Conversely a thin category determines a preorder; it determines a partial order on its objects if it is skeletal. Its nondegenerate nerve consists of strict finite chains.
reconstruction: Antisymmetry, or equivalently passage to a skeleton, is missing from the stated converse. Two distinct isomorphic objects in a thin category contradict that converse literally.
fate: \citet[\S2]{segal1968classifying}; \citet[\S1]{quillen1973higher}. Both precede the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: A group as a one-object category
notes: A group gives the opposite extreme: one object, group elements as morphisms, and group multiplication as composition.
statement: For a discrete group \(G\), the one-object category with automorphism group \(G\) has \(N_kG=G^k\). Its realization is a model of \(BG\).
reconstruction: The discrete case is used here, consistently with the later universal-cover assertion; a topological group requires a topological nerve and different homotopy-group statements.
fate: \citet[\S3]{segal1968classifying}. Compare 1973-308.12.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: A contractible-cover model for a space
notes: For an open cover \(\{U_\alpha\}\), intersections are unions of cover members; order is inclusion. If the sets are contractible, the notes assert \(|\mathcal C|\simeq X\), followed by \ru{Добавл. пересечения}.
statement: A sufficient precise version is the nerve theorem for a numerable good open cover of a paracompact space: every nonempty finite intersection is contractible, and \(X\) is homotopy equivalent to the nerve. The category of nonempty finite indexed intersections, ordered by reverse inclusion of index sets, realizes its barycentric subdivision.
reconstruction: This is a sufficient good-cover reconstruction, not a proof of the more general basis-like formulation in the notes. Numerability, finite-intersection hypotheses, and retention of intersection labels are explicit additions.
fate: \citet[\S4, Proposition 4.1]{segal1968classifying} supplies the numerable-cover comparison (1968).
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The sphere and the octahedral order complex
notes: Two hemispherical sets have an annular intersection \(w\), so the three-object diagram gives only an interval. Splitting \(w=W_1\cup W_2\) and its overlap into two components produces the drawn octahedral surface.
statement: Take six contractible open sets in three levels \(\{U,V\}\), \(\{W_1,W_2\}\), \(\{X_1,X_2\}\), each lower-level set included in each higher-level set and no other strict inclusions. Their order complex is \(S^0*S^0*S^0\cong S^2\), the octahedral boundary.
reconstruction: The written \(x_i\in(W_1\cap W_2)_{\rm comp}\) are interpreted as component labels; actual open components, rather than selected points, are required for this cover argument. The schematic diagram does not specify a unique cover.
fate: The cover method is in \citet[\S4]{segal1968classifying}; the six-element model is directly reconstructed from the page.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The spherical building of a vector space
notes: For a finite-dimensional vector space over any field, the category of proper subspaces and inclusions is called its building.
statement: For a field \(K\) and \(n=\dim_KV\geq2\), let \(\mathcal B(V)=\{W:0<W<V\}\), ordered by inclusion. Its order complex is the spherical building of type \(A_{n-1}\). Both zero and \(V\) are excluded.
reconstruction: The exclusion of zero is supplied by the subsequent definition \(0<W\leq H\) on the same page. Including zero would make the nerve contractible.
fate: \citet[Example 8.2 and end of \S8]{quillen1978poset} checks the model; \citet{tits1974buildings} expanded the 1968 seminar notes in 1974. Compare 1973-321.5.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The Solomon--Tits homotopy type
notes: The building is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres of dimension \(n-2\). The number depends on the field and is infinite for an infinite field.
statement: For \(n\geq2\), \(|\mathcal B(V)|\simeq\bigvee_I S^{n-2}\). For \(K=\mathbb F_q\), \(|I|=q^{\binom n2}\); for an infinite field the index set is infinite. Wedges carry their CW topology, and \(S^0\) is a pointed two-point set.
reconstruction: \ours{} The finite-field count makes the notebook's field-dependence explicit: hyperplanes not containing a fixed line number \(q^{n-1}\), so the induction gives \(r_n=q^{n-1}r_{n-1}\), \(r_2=q\). The same induction gives infinitely many summands for an infinite field.
fate: \citet[Example 8.2 and pp.117--118]{quillen1978poset} gives a later proof of the established theorem. The notebook attributes it to Solomon--Tits, not to new work of Segal.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: A maximum contracts a poset nerve
notes: If an ordered set has a maximum, its realization is contractible; a cone is drawn.
statement: If a nonempty poset \(P\) has a maximum \(m\), each simplex extends to a simplex with vertex \(m\); hence \(|P|\) is a cone. More generally, an initial or terminal object contracts a category's nerve.
reconstruction: The general categorical version is contextual; the page needs only the maximum case.
fate: \citet[\S1, Proposition 2, Corollary 2]{quillen1973higher}. Earlier occurrence: 1973-309.5.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The cover by hyperplane cones
notes: The maximal elements are hyperplanes; \(|\mathcal C|=\bigcup_H|\mathcal C_H|\), where \(\mathcal C_H=\{W:0<W\leq H\}\); each member is contractible.
statement: Each \(|\mathcal C_H|\) is a cone on \(H\). Every finite proper-subspace flag has its largest member contained in a hyperplane, so these simplicial subcomplexes cover \(|\mathcal B(V)|\).
reconstruction: The pieces are subcomplexes, not asserted to be open subsets.
fate: The contraction is checked by \citet[\S1, Proposition 2]{quillen1973higher}; compare the dual line-cover proof in \citet[end of \S8]{quillen1978poset}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: Contracting the fixed-line part of the building
notes: Fix a line \(L\), and put \(Y=\bigcup_{H\supset L}|\mathcal C_H|\). The notes contract \(Y\) using intersections of the cone cover.
statement: Let \(P_L=\{0<W<V:W+L<V\}\). Then \(Y=|P_L|\). The order-preserving map \(W\mapsto W+L\) satisfies \(W\leq W+L\geq L\); realization is homotopic both to the identity and to the constant map at \(L\), contracting \(Y\).
reconstruction: \ours{} This direct order-homotopy argument supplies the finite-intersection step for arbitrary fields and arbitrary numbers of hyperplanes.
fate: \citet[\S1, Proposition 2]{quillen1973higher} supplies the homotopy principle. The particular contraction is reconstructed from the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The nonempty finite-intersection criterion
notes: If all finite intersections of the covering pieces are contractible and nonempty, their union is contractible. The words excluding an empty intersection are partly overwritten but visible.
statement: For a numerable open good cover, or a cover of a simplicial complex by subcomplexes, suppose the intersection of every nonempty finite subfamily is nonempty and contractible. The nerve is then a full simplex and the union is contractible.
reconstruction: The requirement concerns every finite subfamily, not merely those whose intersection happens to be nonempty. The cover topology is supplied. The subcomplex version applies to the building.
fate: The nerve argument is used in \citet[end of \S8]{quillen1978poset}; the open-cover comparison is in \citet[\S4]{segal1968classifying}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: Collapsing the common part gives a wedge
notes: Lemma 1: if \(X=Y\cup Y_1\cup\cdots\cup Y_k\), all pieces are contractible and \(Y_i\cap Y_j\subset Y\) for distinct indices, then \(X\simeq\bigvee_iY_i/(Y_i\cap Y)\).
statement: Let \(X\) be a CW complex covered by subcomplexes \(Y,Y_i\), with \(Y\) nonempty contractible, \(Y_i\cap Y\ne\varnothing\), and \(Y_i\cap Y_j\subset Y\) for \(i\ne j\). Then \(X\to X/Y\) is a homotopy equivalence and \(X/Y\cong\bigvee_iY_i/(Y_i\cap Y)\). Contractibility of the \(Y_i\) is used in the next step.
reconstruction: CW/cofibration and nonempty-intersection hypotheses are added. The result extends to arbitrary families of subcomplexes with CW weak topology, as required over an infinite field.
fate: This elementary quotient fact is used in the 1974 talk. A modern check is \citet[Proposition 0.17]{hatcher2002algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: A cofiber in a contractible space is a suspension
notes: Lemma 2 states \(Z/Z_0\simeq SZ_0\) when \(Z\) is contractible and \(Z_0\subset Z\); cone and suspension diagrams explain the replacement.
statement: For a CW pair \((Z,Z_0)\) with \(Z\) contractible and \(Z_0\ne\varnothing\), the quotient is homotopy equivalent to the unreduced suspension \(SZ_0\). Use the mapping cone of the inclusion, which is nullhomotopic.
reconstruction: The cofibration condition and nonemptiness qualify the unqualified subset notation.
fate: A later precise reference for this established cofiber fact is \citet[Examples 0.13--0.14]{hatcher2002algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The hyperplane intersection and dimension induction
notes: Lemma 3 identifies \(|\mathcal C_H|\cap Y\) with the building of \(H\), yielding reduction by dimension.
statement: If \(H\) does not contain \(L\), then \(\mathcal C_H\cap P_L=\{W:0<W<H\}\). Indeed \(H+L=V\), while \(W<H\) implies \(\dim(W+L)\leq n-1\). For \(n\geq3\), the preceding decomposition therefore gives \(|\mathcal B(V)|\simeq\bigvee_{H\not\supset L} S|\mathcal B(H)|\).
reconstruction: \ours{} The condition \(H\not\supset L\) is restored from the preceding line. For distinct such hyperplanes, \(\dim(H\cap H')=n-2\), so their cone intersection lies in \(Y\), as required. The base case is separate.
fate: This is the notebook's proof of the theorem checked in \citet[\S8]{quillen1978poset}; that source uses a different, dual cover proof.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The dimension-two base case
notes: The first induction step is \(\dim V=2\), where the building is a collection of points (lines); the phrase about a wedge is overwritten.
statement: For \(\dim_KV=2\), \(|\mathcal B(V)|=\mathbb P^1(K)\) with the discrete topology. A chosen base line identifies it with a wedge of copies of \(S^0\), one for every remaining line. Over \(\mathbb F_q\) there are \(q+1\) points and \(q\) copies of \(S^0\).
reconstruction: \ours{} A wedge of one-point spaces would be a point; the intended spheres are pointed two-point spaces. This also fixes the homology convention below.
fate: The base case agrees with \citet[Example 8.2]{quillen1978poset} and is directly visible in the row of points.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: Suspending a wedge of spheres
notes: The suspension of a wedge of spheres is again a wedge of spheres.
statement: For a based CW complex \(A=\bigvee_I S^d\), \(d\geq0\), the reduced suspension is \(\Sigma A\cong\bigvee_I S^{d+1}\). The unreduced suspension \(SA\) is homotopy equivalent to \(\Sigma A\), by collapsing the basepoint interval.
reconstruction: The based CW convention includes the disconnected \(d=0\) case in the induction.
fate: The standard argument is checked in \citet[Example 0.10]{hatcher2002algebraic}; the notebook uses it in 1974.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The Steinberg module and reduced homology
notes: The displayed line identifies \(H_{n-2}(|\mathcal C|;\mathbb Z)\) with the Steinberg module of \(V\).
statement: The integral Steinberg module is \(\operatorname{St}(V)=\widetilde H_{n-2}(|\mathcal B(V)|;\mathbb Z)\), with its natural \(\operatorname{GL}(V)\)-action. For \(n\geq3\), ordinary and reduced homology agree in this degree; for \(n=2\), reduced homology is necessary.
reconstruction: \ours{} Over \(\mathbb F_q\) in dimension two, ordinary \(H_0\) has rank \(q+1\), while the reduced group has rank \(q\). The literal formula fails at the base case retained in this talk.
fate: The building interpretation belongs to the older Solomon--Tits theory; \citet[\S\S8--9]{quillen1978poset} checks its reduced-homology dimension.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The classifying space of a discrete group is aspherical
notes: For the category of a group, \(|\mathcal C|=BG\), \(\pi_1(|\mathcal C|)=G\), and the universal covering is contractible.
statement: For a discrete group \(G\), the nerve realization \(BG\) is a connected CW complex with \(\pi_1(BG)\cong G\) and \(\pi_k(BG)=0\) for \(k>1\).
reconstruction: Discreteness is essential: for a well-behaved topological group the usual formula is \(\pi_k(BG)\cong\pi_{k-1}(G)\), not asphericity in general.
fate: \citet[\S3]{segal1968classifying}, published six years before this exposition.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The contractible chaotic category
notes: \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}\) has objects the elements of \(G\) and one morphism between every ordered pair. Its realization is called contractible because every element is linked to \(1\).
statement: The unique morphisms \(g\to1\) form a natural transformation from the identity functor to the constant functor at \(1\). Realization gives a contraction. Simplices are arbitrary finite strings of elements of \(G\).
reconstruction: Connectedness of a graph alone is insufficient; coherent higher simplices and the natural transformation give the actual argument.
fate: \citet[\S3 and Proposition 2.1]{segal1968classifying}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The universal-cover functor and multiplication convention
notes: The functor sends each object to the unique object and \(g\to g'\) to \(g^{-1}g'\). Its realization is the universal covering.
statement: Adopt the convention that a path labelled first \(a\), then \(b\), has composite label \(ab\). Then \((g^{-1}g')(g'^{-1}g'')=g^{-1}g''\), so this is a functor. Left multiplication on strings by discrete \(G\) gives a principal covering \(EG\to BG\), with \(EG\) the contractible realization of the chaotic category.
reconstruction: An opposite composition convention requires changing the formula consistently. The scan is not emended merely because conventions differ.
fate: \citet[\S3]{segal1968classifying} gives the construction and the extra local-triviality issue for general topological groups.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: Transition functions and a bundle's classifying map
notes: A bundle \(E\to X\), a trivializing cover, intersections, and \(X\to BG\) are drawn. The last sentence about the intersection category stops before completing the construction.
statement: For a numerable principal \(G\)-bundle over a paracompact base, continuous transition functions define a functor from the topological \v{C}ech category, retaining points in intersections, to the one-object topological category \(G\). Realization and the cover equivalence give the classifying map up to homotopy, using a standard numerable universal-bundle model.
reconstruction: The completion is editorial. The notes do not specify discrete versus topological \(G\), a principal bundle, or how point-dependent transitions enter the functor. A category of unlabelled open sets alone cannot encode arbitrary transition functions.
fate: The completion was published in \citet[\S4, Proposition 4.1]{segal1968classifying}; the surviving final sentence is a partial match.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; this occurrence supplies no unresolved problem.

title: The total Milnor number of a polynomial
notes: For \(P:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C\), all critical points are assumed isolated. The question is how to count them with multiplicities.
statement:
When the gradient ideal has finite colength, the finite sum of local critical-point multiplicities is
\[\begin{aligned}
\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}(P)
 &=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(P_{z_1},\ldots,P_{z_n})\\
 &=\sum_{a\in\operatorname{Crit}(P)}\mu_a(P).
\end{aligned}\] The question is to bound and generically compute this number from the support of \(P\).
fate: The equality with the sum of local algebras is \citet[\S\S4--5]{kushnirenko1975newton}; the ensuing Newton bound is its TheoremII. The paper was received 30 September 1974 and published 1975; the notebook records the global discussion on21 October 1974.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

pages: P000579, convex hull and two inequalities
title: The Newton upper bound and equality at infinity
notes: Take the convex hull of 0 and the exponents with nonzero coefficients. In two dimensions the count is at most \(2S-a-b+1\), with equality under nondegeneracy.
statement: Let \(P\) have a finite critical locus and be convenient, so its support meets every coordinate axis. For \(\Delta_\infty=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\operatorname{supp}P)\), define \(\nu_\infty\) by the same alternating sum of coordinate-section volumes as in record 346. Then \(\sum\mu_a(P)\le\nu_\infty\). Equality holds if every face at infinity is nondegenerate in the logarithmic-derivative sense; in that case the critical locus is finite. In dimension 2 this is \(2S-a-b+1\).
reconstruction: Convenience and nondegeneracy on every relevant face at infinity are supplied; arbitrary support or a single tested face does not justify the formula.
fate: Exact match with \citet[TheoremII(i)--(iii)]{kushnirenko1975newton}, including genericity at fixed support; \citet{kouchnirenko1976polyedres} gives the full treatment. This upper bound and the local lower bound concern different Newton regions and are compatible.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Global multiplicity as the degree of the normalized gradient
notes: The map on \(|z|=R\) sends \(z\) to \((P_{z_1},\ldots,P_{z_n})/|\operatorname{grad}P|\); the sum of Milnor numbers equals its degree.
statement: Choose \(R\) so every isolated critical point lies strictly inside the ball and the gradient is nonzero on its boundary. With complex orientations, \(\deg(\nabla P/\|\nabla P\|:S_R^{2n-1}\to S^{2n-1})=\sum_a\mu_a(P)\). This is additivity of the degree of a holomorphic map with isolated zeros. It does not require the gradient to be a proper map of all of \(\mathbb C^n\).
fate: The local and global degree interpretation is stated explicitly in \citet[\S1.1, Eqs.~(1)--(3), p.~2]{kouchnirenko1976polyedres}, which credits the established singularity theory preceding the talk. Compare \citet[\S7]{milnor1968singular} and the support-dependent count in \citet[\S\S4--5]{kushnirenko1975newton}. The notebook uses the degree principle as a proof idea, not as a new independent theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Normal cone semigroup algebras are Cohen--Macaulay
notes: The ring of monomials whose exponents lie in a cone is said to be Cohen--Macaulay; Melvin Hochster is named at the head of the page.
statement: For a rational polyhedral cone \(\sigma\subset\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n\), the saturated finitely generated semigroup \(\sigma\cap\mathbb Z^n\) defines a normal affine semigroup ring \(\mathbb C[\sigma\cap\mathbb Z^n]\), and this ring is Cohen--Macaulay. Saturation is a hypothesis, not a consequence for an arbitrary selected set of monomial generators.
fate: \citet[main theorem, p.~318]{hochster1972invariants}, published September 1972. This is the same proof ingredient already mentioned in 1974-346.6; the second occurrence is retained because the global counting argument invokes it explicitly.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Toric compactifications as the geometric interpretation
notes: The final line before Polyakov says only \ru{Мамфорд --- торич. вложения}.
statement: The identifiable method is to treat the cone monomial rings as affine charts of toric varieties and use a toric compactification adapted to the Newton polytope. No particular fan, compactification theorem or intersection formula is specified on this page.
fate: The connection is consistent with the toric proof language of the Newton-polyhedron literature, including \citet[proof of the theorem]{khovanskii1978eulerjacobi}. That is a thematic comparison only; this isolated name does not identify a distinct theorem of Mumford or justify a new open-problem entry.
present_status: As of November 2026, the toric-geometric method is identifiable, but the exact Mumford result intended by this isolated line is not. No mathematical question is stated.

title: The Yang--Mills curvature-squared action
notes: The displayed action contains \(\partial_\alpha b_{\alpha\beta}-\partial_\beta b_\alpha-[b_\alpha,b_\beta]^2\) inside an incomplete trace parenthesis.
statement: Fix a compact Lie group, an invariant positive inner product on its Lie algebra, and a connection \(A=\sum_\alpha A_\alpha dx^\alpha\) on Euclidean four-space. In the convention \(F_A=dA+A\wedge A\), \(F_{\alpha\beta}=\partial_\alpha A_\beta-\partial_\beta A_\alpha+[A_\alpha,A_\beta]\), and \(S(A)=(2g^2)^{-1}\int\langle F_A,F_A\rangle\,d^4x\), for fields for which the integral exists. A change of Lie-algebra convention may change the commutator sign, but the whole curvature is squared.
reconstruction: The invariant inner product, Euclidean convention and full outer square are editorial repairs. No existence theorem for the quantized theory is present.
fate: \citet[Eq.~(4) and the field-equations section]{yangmills1954conservation} gives the curvature and invariant Lagrangian. The theory predates this lecture by twenty years. The manuscript display cannot literally be a curvature-squared action and requires an explicit emendation.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Gauge potentials as local connection forms
notes: An element of a Lie algebra at every point is identified with a connection; taking the coefficients to be Christoffel symbols gives the curvature tensor. The fibre is called a Lie algebra, with SU(2) named as example.
statement: A connection is locally a Lie-algebra-valued one-form, not merely one Lie-algebra element at each point. On overlaps its local forms obey the affine gauge-transformation law. Its curvature is a two-form valued in the adjoint bundle; the analogous construction for a linear connection on the tangent bundle yields the Riemann curvature tensor. The Lie algebra for the named group is \(\mathfrak{su}(2)\).
reconstruction: The one-form index, overlap law and distinction between SU(2) and its Lie algebra correct the notebook\textquotesingle s compressed dictionary.
fate: The standard connection-curvature dictionary is reviewed in \citet[\S2, Eq.~(2.10)]{chernsimons1974characteristic}; Yang--Mills gauge covariance is already in \citet[Eq.~(3)]{yangmills1954conservation}. Both are earlier than 21 October 1974.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The quadratic curvature form representing a Pontryagin class
notes: The contracted expression \(R^b_{a,\delta_1\delta_2}R^a_{b,\delta_3\delta_4}\) is labelled a Pontryagin class.
statement: For a real vector bundle with a metric connection and skew-symmetric curvature matrix \(\Omega\), the closed four-form \(-\tfrac1{8\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}(\Omega\wedge\Omega)\) represents the real image of \(p_1\). The written component contraction supplies the coefficient pattern only after alternating the four differential indices. title: A spatially uniform irreducible current-group representation
notes: Gelfand asks whether there is an irreducible representation \ru{которое всюду устроено одинаково}.
statement: For \(X=[0,1]\), \(G=PSL_2(\mathbb R)\), and a positive multiple \(m=\lambda\,dx\) of Lebesgue measure, construct a nontrivial irreducible strongly continuous representation of \(C(X,G)\) whose equivalence class is invariant under measure-preserving transformations of \(X\) that act on the chosen current group by pullback. This full-support condition excludes finite sets of evaluation points and follows from the positive measure on every such interval in the construction.

title: The isometric diagonal delta embedding
notes: The intertwiner is written \(f(t)\mapsto f(t)\delta(t-s)\), labelled a unitary embedding.

title: The scalar cocycle restoring unitarity

title: One-sided analytic continuation and directional regularity

title: Gelfand proposes polynomial as well as linear integration
notes: \ru{Идея Г.} is followed by integrating linear functions and polynomials; a curved outline is cut by parallel segments.
statement: The evidence supports a proposal to replace linear level sets by polynomial ones in an integral-geometric construction. It does not identify the family of polynomials, the integration measure, a target space, or an inversion or range question. Thus it determines no unique theorem or problem.
fate: Generalized Radon transforms are thematically related to the canonical-relation calculus of \citet[\S4.1]{hormander1971fourier}, but that relation does not identify this particular proposal. The scan does not justify reading the small sketch as a specified polynomial transform.
present_status: As of November 2026: the precise intended construction is not recoverable from this entry; no claim of an undeveloped idea is made.
